nodes.label: A1.1 · Blower Building Plan
nodes.status: Available · Read method Visual (rev1) · Addendum 4: Reissued — Add. 4 p.4 governs
nodes.summary: The Blower Building is one room (Room 101, Blower Room, FF=23.30); Add. 4 resizes it from 42.00' × 9.50' to 44.00' × 9.25' [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 4 and p.4 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Add. 4 extends the new slab 9" north to abut the existing Train 2 building slab, has the Contractor field-measure and match the Train 2 finished floor, and states about 9" clearance between the buildings with the 10-ft setback kept from the south and east property lines [Add. 4 p.3, p.4 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The base plan shows four blowers on a concrete blower pad 22.60' long and 4.50' deep (3" typical blower-to-pad edge) set 6.00' from the west wall (7.00' per Add. 4), an electrical panel bank with a 3.5-ft clearance note, two Ø24" bladder tanks per 1/C4.3, a 36"×84" motorized louver and a 24"×24" manual louver on the west wall, and two 24"×24" vents with exhaust fans on the east wall [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.4 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Add. 4 moves the MCC as far east as possible and adds a section (eight 20" sections, 160", spare section for future expansion), moves the MCP panel and its raceways, relocates the 2W bladder tank assembly per C6.4, and calls for 2 fire extinguisher assemblies (base shows 1) at wall locations coordinated with the Owner [Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 4, p.3, p.4 — Verified; plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 governs]. The door schedule lists insulated hollow-metal, painted doors 101A (two pairs, 10'-0"×8'-0"×1-3/4", Type B), 101B (3'-0" wide, Type A; height illegible at stored resolution) and 101C (5'-0"×8'-0"×1-3/4", Type A) with no hardware group, and the finish schedule with Details 1–2 calls for a sealed concrete floor, 6" rubber base, painted GWB walls, painted exposed-structure ceiling, and R-25 wall / R-30 roof fiberglass insulation with vapor barrier and board on furring channels at 24" o.c. [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; 101B height — Unresolved: need native sheet].

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.54 (plans_7 p.6); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 3 p.6 (set p.54); Wiki note A1.2 (Project_Wiki.md line 785)
nodes.label: A1.2 · Blower Building Exterior Elevations 1
nodes.status: Available · Read method Visual (rev1) · Addendum 4: Reissued — Add. 4 p.5 governs
nodes.summary: The four elevations show a single-slope (1:12) metal building with X-braced walls on a concrete foundation; Add. 4 changes the length from 42.00' to 44.00' and the width from 9.50' to 9.25' [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.5 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Add. 4 raises the building so both through-wall exhaust fans clear, taking the east-elevation minimum haunch height clearance from 9.00' to 10.25' and the floor-to-vent dimension from 6.75' to 8.00' [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.5 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The conceptual framing view (not to scale) has the Contractor provide a pre-engineered metal building with a similar column and bracing layout; Add. 4 sets a semi-flush girt at the high sidewall (5" from outside of column flange to outside of Zee girt flange), bypass Zee girts on all other sides, and Contractor means and methods for a weather-tight north wall with exterior metal panels that may be built on the ground and lifted into place [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.3 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The south elevation shows door 101C at 5.00' × 8'-0", two door pairs of 5.00' leaves, and door 101B at 3.00' × 6'-8"; the west elevation shows the 7.00'-tall motorized louver and a 2.00' × 2.00' louver [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual]. A footing-perimeter note calls for R-10 extruded polystyrene from top of concrete to bottom of footing, top chamfered 45°, exposed faces covered with grey Dryvit EIFS or equal, and metal-building-color flashing lapped at least 3" over the board [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.55 (plans_7 p.7); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 3 p.7 (set p.55); Wiki note A1.3 (Project_Wiki.md line 799)
nodes.label: A1.3 · Building Details
nodes.summary: Interior elevations of the proposed Blower Building show the four blowers, and the general note leaves process air and 2W piping off for clarity, pointing to civil sheets C1.1, C6.4 and C6.5 [plans_7 p.7 — Verified (labels); Verified-Visual (note, elevations)]. At the existing office building, the existing 4'-0" × 4'-0" louvered vent (south elevation) and 2' × 3' louvered vent (east elevation) are removed, the metal siding is replaced floor to eave with continuous siding to match (no horizontal seams), and the existing generator exhaust assembly is removed [plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual]. At the existing WWTP building, a new 3' × 7' louvered vent and a new 2' × 2' (24" × 24") exhaust fan are framed in, trimmed to match existing louvers and caulked, each marked "typical for all three locations," with final locations coordinated with the Owner [plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual]. Existing wall heights are shown as 9.50'± and the new exhaust fan is set 6.00' above the concrete slab floor [plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: C0.1 · Existing Conditions
nodes.summary: Existing-conditions plan of the WWTP parcel showing the Eastsound Water District office building (FF 23.5), the existing treatment plant (two circular tanks), the screw press room, a concrete retaining wall, chain-link fence with gate, and 10-ft building setback lines (plans_1 p.8, C0.1 — Verified-Visual). Parcel boundaries and easements shown include a 5-ft easement to the Port (AFN 2002 0701021), a 20-ft easement (AFN 107644 plus a second number, partly legible), and a 10-ft easement noted as approximate location and as-constructed (plans_1 p.8, C0.1 — Verified-Visual). The storm structure table lists DCB 1072 and DCB 1076 (Type I) and DMH 1287 (48-in pump-out manhole); the sewer structure table lists SSMH 1285 (septic tank), SSMH 1286 (sewage pump), SSMH 1288 and SSMH 2258, each with rim and invert data (plans_1 p.8, C0.1 — Verified-Visual). Other existing features: 8-in PVC influent sample port (IE 19.4), concrete fuel tank basin, pad-mounted transformer, generator, shed, and hangars on adjoining Port of Orcas parcels (plans_1 p.8, C0.1 — Verified-Visual). Labels 'WSE #205, #206, #208, #211' and 'TB-1' to 'TB-3' appear with no stated meaning on the sheet (plans_1 p.8, C0.1 — Verified-Visual).

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.9 (Pages_from_eswd-wwtp-upgrade-ph1-11x17-plans_2Part-1.pdf p.1); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 1 p.9 (set p.9); Wiki note C0.2 (Project_Wiki.md line 381)
nodes.label: C0.2 · T.E.S.C. Narrative
nodes.summary: Construction stormwater narrative organized by the 13 required elements (clearing limits, construction access, flow rates, sediment controls, soil stabilization, slopes, drain inlets, channels and outlets, pollutants, dewatering, BMP maintenance, project management, low-impact-development BMPs) plus general notes on BMP installation, maintenance and removal (plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Project description: total project area 0.45 ac, proposed impervious area 0.04 ac, area to be disturbed 0.30 ac, estimated cut 3,382 CY and fill 1,596 CY, stated as for the TESC narrative only and not for bidding or take-off (Item 15; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). The site is mostly flat, with grass turf along the north and south property lines and no trees or shrubs; runoff flows southeast to northwest into a ditch on the adjoining site along the north boundary; there are no streams, lakes, wetlands, residential or critical areas; soils are mapped as Roche-Killebrew complex, 2 to 10 percent slopes (Items 16–21; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Sequence: install silt fence, construction entrance and inlet protection; remove pavement for sewer structures; clear and grade for the building addition and retaining wall; build them; install stormwater conveyance; pave and stabilize landscape areas (Item 22; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Construction is expected from spring 2023 to fall 2024; no sediment ponds, diversions or waterways are used and no detention calculations are needed (Items 23–24; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual).

nodes.label: C0.4 · T.E.S.C. Details
nodes.summary: Five TESC details, all not to scale: 1 Plastic Covering for Slopes & Stockpiles, 2 Catch Basin Insert, 3 Filter Fabric Fence, 4 Stabilized Construction Entrance, 5 Geotextile Encased Check Dam (BMP C208) (plans_2Part-3 p.1, C0.4 — Verified; detail numbers Verified-Visual). Plastic covering is 6-mil minimum with 12-in seam overlap and toes buried in 4x6-in trenches; catch basin inserts go in before clearing and grading and are emptied when half full (Details 1–2 notes; plans_2Part-3 p.1, C0.4 — Verified-Visual). The construction entrance is 4–8-in quarry spalls on geotextile, 12 in minimum thick and 100 ft minimum long, based on Figure II-3.1 of the 2019 Stormwater Management Manual for Western Washington (Detail 4; plans_2Part-3 p.1, C0.4 — Verified-Visual). The filter fabric fence defers to WSDOT Standard Plans I-30.10-02 or I-30.15-02 (high-visibility fence I-30.16-01 or I-30.17-01), and the check dam notes defer to 'Standard Specifications' 8-01.3(6)A, 9-14.5(4) and 8-01.3(15) (Details 3, 5; plans_2Part-3 p.1, C0.4 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). The Contractor is responsible for updating coverage under Ecology's Construction Stormwater General Permit (Detail 5 note; plans_2Part-3 p.1, C0.4 — Verified-Visual).

nodes.label: C0.5 · Demolition Plan
nodes.status: Available · Read method Visual · Addendum 4: Cited — Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 1
nodes.summary: Demolition plan with 25 keyed notes covering removal of existing pipe (40 LF 8-in and 60 LF 10-in effluent/outfall, 40 LF 4-in roof drain, 87 LF storm drain with a catch basin, 20 LF 6-in drain, 60 LF 1-1/2-in sump force main, 7 ft and 8 LF of storm drain, and the 8-in influent pipe), 149 LF and 119 LF of chain link fence, 61 LF of retaining wall, and the generator fuel tank with its concrete spill basin (Keyed Notes 1–2, 8–9, 11–12, 16–21, 24; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). Removals follow their replacements: the effluent pipes come out after the interim 8-in HDPE pipe (C0.7) is installed and tested, the sump pump station and its piping after the new plant drain pump station, and the septic tank (SSMH 1285) after the new septic tank and influent pump station, with temporary pumps, piping and basins as needed (Keyed Notes 1, 3–5, 8, 11–12; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). The Contractor keeps the 2-in water service and sump station power live until replacements are tested, protects the storm drain pump station manhole (DMH 1287), potholes storm, power and telecom before new work, relocates existing holding tanks on site per Owner, and sawcuts asphalt pavement (Keyed Notes 5–6, 10, 13–15, 25; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). Construction phasing and the demolition schedule cover the existing basin: remove the 8-in slab over the original pre-aeration basin by saw cut near the building's east face, remove fill while supporting internal piping, bypass all flow during a time-critical step, complete a checklist (walls, coatings, penetrations, three weir gates) before accepting wastewater, and remove internal piping after the new flow splitter is operational (Construction Phasing 1–5, Demolition Schedule 1–3; plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual). A demolition plan with schedule must be approved by the Engineer before any demolition; Add. 4 states saw-cut information is on C0.5 but new surfacing information is on C2.6, which is unavailable — Add. 4 governs (General Note, plans_2Part-4 p.1, C0.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 1 — Verified).

nodes.label: C3.1 · Influent Flow Splitter Site Plan
nodes.norm_label: c3.1 · influent flow splitter site plan
nodes.summary: Plan of the new flow splitter box beside existing Train #1, with 8" outlets to Train #1 (west), Train #2 and Train #3 (south), a future Train #4 connection sealed with an 8" blind flange (keyed note 1), and the inlet from the north; dashed vaults with flow meter symbols sit on the inlet line and on the Train #2 and Train #3 lines, and a vault drain is labeled. Keyed notes: proposed concrete support for the splitter box (2); existing sampling port (3); pipe supports per 5/C7.2 (4); carefully cut a hole through the building for the new 8" Train #1 influent and seal with flashing (5); 8" Train #1 influent elbow discharging into the aeration basin beside the existing influent pipe (7); confirm the existing Train #2 influent pipe and connect new 8" DI piping with positive drainage from the splitter box (8); pot-hole existing 8" piping before construction (9). Construction sequence: install the new splitter box and piping to Trains #1 and #3 without disturbing existing piping and operations; when complete and tested, connect the 8" influent to the new influent pump station and direct flow to Trains #1 and #3; then dewater, abandon and remove existing influent piping conflicts so the Train #2 piping and flow meter vault can be installed. Train #2 downtime is limited to 5 days max (Monday–Friday).

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.27 (Pages_from_eswd-wwtp-upgrade-ph1-11x17-plans_4Part-3.pdf p.1); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 1 p.27 (set p.27); Wiki note C3.2 (Project_Wiki.md line 528)
nodes.label: C3.2 · Influent Flow Splitter Elevations
nodes.summary: Keyed note 7 makes the flow splitter a prefabricated 316 SS unit sized to match the drawing, with 4 equal splitter chambers (flow to each of the 3 trains and 1 additional train), an adjustable weir in each chamber and a removable cover; manufacturer Smith & Loveless or approved equal. The box is about 7'-0" × 4'-6" in plan (outlet spacing 5'-3") with its bottom at elev 26.00 on a proposed concrete support about 6.5' × 4.0' × 1.3' tall; the contractor coordinates the support with the actual box, top of concrete elev 26.00, see structural drawings (keyed note 2); the existing slab TOC is 24.7. The inlet is 6" DI restrained pipe and a restrained 90° bend (INV 20.75) rising through a 12"×6" DI eccentric reducer, 12" DI flange spools and 90° bends on 12" pipe supports per 5/C7.2; outlets are 8" DI flanged bends and spools (one at INV 20.75) on 8" pipe supports per 5/C7.2, labeled To Cell #1, #2 and #3, with a future connection sealed by a blind flange (keyed note 1). A manually adjustable weir is configured to fine-tune an even split among all four outlet pipes.

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.28 (Pages_from_eswd-wwtp-upgrade-ph1-11x17-plans_4Part-4.pdf p.1); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 2 p.1 (set p.28); Wiki note C3.3 (Project_Wiki.md line 538)
nodes.label: C3.3 · Train 3 Plan
nodes.summary: Plan of the new Train 3 bullseye tank: 32.00' inner and 34.00' outer wall diameter, 12" walls and a 12" footing extension, around an 18'-0" clarifier (R300, 500.7 SF) with a 5'-0" feed well, sludge scraper arms and scraper arm drive, skimmer arm, scum skimmer airlift, a 3'-0" clarifier bridge and a 2' peripheral clarifier walkway with handrail. The annulus holds Aeration Zone #1 (3,983 CF), Aeration Zone #2 (1,322 CF), Anoxic Zone #1 (2,097 CF) and Anoxic Zone #2 (1,175 CF), with plenum diffusers, an adjustable weir, DO #1 and DO #2 DO/pH sensors (detail 1/C7.4), two submersible mixers, a RAS airlift weir box, a nitrate recycle weir box and a 6" nitrate recycle (MLR) pipe; a 3" RAS airlift sludge duct and a 10" clarifier inlet pipe run inside the clarifier. Connections: Train 3 8" influent IE 20.08, Train 3 8" effluent IE 20.00, 2" WAS/clarifier drain to the WAS pump, and a 6" air inlet. Two davit crane assemblies and a prefab aluminum ladder assembly connected to the access platform (clarifier bridge) are shown; note 1 requires partitions reinforced for individual zone dewatering (not shown for clarity).

nodes.label: C4.1 · Influent Pump Station
nodes.summary: The new Influent Pump Station is a 96" precast wet well "per WSDOT Std Plan B-15.60-00 for precast manholes" (Unresolved: external reference, not staged) on a 12" thick precast base, interior bottom elev 9.0 and top elev 23.30, with the top slab per 1/S2.4 and 2/S2.4, a 36"×36" Halliday H1R3636 hatch and a 30"×48" Halliday H1R3048 hatch over the pumps (both H-20), and "WrapidSeal or equal" at all joints; it takes 8" influent at IE 19.50, 4" filtrate and digester supernatant at IE 13.40 and a 4" sample sump line at IE 18.00. Small and large pumps, each a duplex arrangement per specs (keyed notes 28, 52, 53), hang on stainless guide rails with stainless haul chains, manufacturer's disconnect elbows and flapper valves that close and seal when submerged; discharges pass through two precast valve vaults (4'-2" × 4'-2" × 5'-6" minimum inside, Utility Vault Co. 506-LA or equal, floor elev 18.0±) with 4" and 6" check and gate valves and pressure gages, into 4" and 6" DI restrained piping with buried gate valves. Floats F1–F4 on timer control start the redundant large lag (19.00), large lead (18.50), small lag (18.00) and small lead (17.50) pumps; the transducer, set 6" above the floor, runs T1 high level alarm 17.50 (with float), T2 large lag 17.00, T3 large lead 16.00, T4 small lag 14.00, T5 small lead 12.00, T6 pumps off 11.00 and T7 low level alarm and redundant off 10.50. Also shown: the influent sample sump structure (see 4/C7.5), a 2" SCH 80 conduit for the influent sampler intake tubing, a 3" stainless vent pipe with 24-mesh stainless screen (IE 21.00), clean outs, 2" PVC and 4" vault drains (IE 16.15), link-seal boots at every pipe-to-concrete penetration, 16 stainless anchor bolts, steps or ladder per WSDOT Std Plan B-30.90-01 (keyed note 21) and a 12" base of Class A gravel per WSDOT 9-03.12(1)A — both Unresolved: external reference, not staged. The vertical pipe brace points to detail 7/C7.2 (keyed note 27) and to "sheet M4.1" (elevation callout), which is not in the sheet index (Issue 11); Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 2 requires CANUSA-CPS WrapidSeal (Manhole Encapsulation System) or approved equal on the exterior of all precast concrete wet well and vault joints, installed per manufacturer, over the C4.1 call-out — Add. 4 governs.

nodes.label: C4.2 · 2W Pump Station Plan & Profile
nodes.summary: The plant water (2W) pump station is a 96" diameter precast wet well (floor 10.00', top 21.50', on a 12" crushed surfacing base course) under a 30" fiberglass wet well and access structure (top 0.2' above FG, 23.1'±) with an insulated fiberglass gasketed lid on stainless bolts and a 38" traffic-rated lid and manhole ring per 3/C7.5. 2W water arrives "from air gap, see C4.3" in 4" SCH 80 PVC at 2% slope (4" inlet IE 19.50; Kor-N-Seal or equal at the wall penetration), while the plan view labels a 6" inlet pipe (Issue 39). Two submersible well pumps per specifications (single-pump duty points 20 gpm @ 380' TDH, 72 gpm @ 150' TDH, 80 gpm @ 85' TDH) each discharge through a 2" high-pressure discharge assembly (ball valve, true union ball check valve, high-pressure flex hose, quick disconnect; Orenco or approved equal) set within 12" of the lid, with a pressure relief valve rated 110 psi or greater within 24" of the wet well top, then 2" SCH 80 PVC and a 2"×3" reducer to 3" HDPE; field-fit brackets steady the flow-induced tower assembly. Floats: F1 high level alarm and redundant valve close 22.00, F2 valve close 20.00, F3 valve open 19.00, F4 low level alarm and pumps off 15.00; a 1" PVC vent is tapped into the basin and run to a field-located point out of the vehicle drive path (coordinate with Owner). Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 2 (exterior of all precast concrete wet well joints sealed with CANUSA-CPS WrapidSeal or approved equal) applies to this precast wet well, where C4.2 calls no joint sealant — Add. 4 governs.

Trenches get 36 in minimum cover over water and sewer mains, pipe-zone gravel bedding and bank-run gravel or select native backfill at 95%, a 2-in metallic detector tape 8–12 in below grade, #10 AWG tracer wire on nonmetallic pipe, and restoration by hydroseed over 4-in topsoil, new crushed surfacing top course, or HMA Class 1/2 in two lifts matching the existing section (4 in minimum) (Detail 2 Keyed Notes A–I; plans_6 p.6, C7.4 — Verified-Visual). Material and paving callouts defer to WSDOT 9-03.9(3), 5-04.2, 9-03.19 and 9-03.12(3) (Detail 2; plans_6 p.6, C7.4 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). The trench drain sits in a concrete surround 8 in each side with #3 at 24 in and four #3 continuous, trench drain 'per specifications' (Detail 5; plans_6 p.6, C7.4 — Verified-Visual). The D.O. probe mounts to handrail with U-bolts and Unistrut per manufacturer, with power, wiring and conduit by the electrical contractor; equipment pads are 8 in wider and longer than the bolt pattern or per architectural drawings (Details 1, 3; plans_6 p.6, C7.4 — Verified-Visual; cross-lane, see Issues).

nodes.label: C7.5 · Civil Details
nodes.summary: Four details, not to scale: 1 Typical Plant Water (2W) Yard Hydrant Stations, 2 Post Hydrant Detail, 3 Traffic Manhole Ring Details (double manhole condition), 4 Influent Sample Sump (plans_6 p.7, C7.5 — Verified; numbering Verified-Visual). 2W yard hydrant stations use a 1-in frost-proof hydrant on a 2-in HDPE supply with a 2-in gate valve and valve box, a free-standing or wall-mounted aluminum hose rack, and a red 'CAUTION: 2W PLANT WATER NON POTABLE' sign; pipe color follows 'Orange Book' standards per 'Section 15051', which is not in the project manual (Detail 1; plans_6 p.7, C7.5 — Verified-Visual; see Issues). The post hydrant ('see plan for size') is fed by a 2-in HDPE line with a buried 2-in gate valve, thrust block, drain rock and concrete collar (Detail 2; plans_6 p.7, C7.5 — Verified-Visual). The double manhole condition uses lightweight composite manholes (Morrison Bros. 418LC-3800 AM or equal, 35-5/16-in minimum ID, locking, gasketed, 55 lb cover) in a 3,000 psi cast-in-place ring on Class A foundation gravel per WSDOT 9-03.12(1)A (Detail 3; plans_6 p.7, C7.5 — Verified-Visual; WSDOT part Unresolved: external reference, not staged). The influent sample sump is a 24-in by 6-ft precast well curb (H2 Precast WC-24 or equal) on a 12-in precast base, top flush with pavement at about 23.50, with 8-in DI gravity in at IE 19.65 (field-confirm), 8-in influent at IE 19.55, a 4-in drain at IE 18.20, a 2-in sampling conduit, and the traffic-rated lid of 3/C7.1 (Detail 4; plans_6 p.7, C7.5 — Verified-Visual).

nodes.summary: Details of Hot Box #1 (flow meter and isolation valve; Detail 1) and Hot Box #2 (air gap piping; Details 2–3), each a locked, insulated, heated enclosure on a 58 x 24 x 4-in, 3,000 psi concrete slab over 6-in gravel base with 6-in crushed surfacing (plans_6 p.8, C7.6 — Verified; details Verified-Visual). Hot Box #1 holds an ASCO Redhat 8221 slow-closing, normally closed 3/4-in solenoid valve (120 VAC, NEMA 4X), a 1-in flow meter 'per electrical design requirements', a Spears S1780 1.25-in check valve, an Orenco 1.25-in FCA flow control assembly with spare orifice plates, manual ball valves and unions (Material List 1–13; plans_6 p.8, C7.6 — Verified-Visual). Hot Box #2 provides a two-pipe-diameter air gap into a funnel draining through 4-in Sch. 80 PVC, in a Hot Box model HB2ST or approved equal (Details 2–3; plans_6 p.8, C7.6 — Verified-Visual). All piping inside both boxes is Sch. 80 PVC, exposed piping gets 90 W, 120 V heat trace and a receptacle, and corrosive surfaces get two coats of epoxy paint (Notes 1–3, Material List 12; plans_6 p.8, C7.6 — Verified-Visual). Add. 4 relocates and reorients the hot boxes on C1.3 but does not reissue C7.6 (Add. 4 p.3 — Verified).

nodes.summary: Plan and elevation of the Train 2 (Detail 1) and Train 3 (Detail 2) flow meter vaults, each a precast concrete vault 4'-2" x 4'-2" x 5'-0" minimum inside (Utility Vault 506-LA or equal) with a 36 x 36-in H-20 single-leaf hatch (Halliday H1R3636) opening south and a Bilco LadderUp (plans_7 p.4, C7.10 — Verified; details Verified-Visual). Pipe inverts are 20.72 (Train 2) and 20.68 (Train 3) over a nominal floor at 19.0 with 1% grout slope to a floor drain (2/C7.1) that drains to the influent pump station; pipe supports follow 5/C7.2 with 18 in minimum clearance (plans_7 p.4, C7.10 — Verified-Visual). Pipe penetrations get Link-Seal boots, steps or ladder must be non-corrosive per WSDOT Standard Plan B-30.90-02 (galvanized not accepted), and the base is 12 in of Class A foundation gravel per Standard Specifications 9-03.12(1)A (plans_7 p.4, C7.10 — Verified-Visual; WSDOT parts Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Add. 4 Clarification 2 requires the exterior of all precast vault joints to be sealed with CANUSA-CPS WrapidSeal or approved equal — Add. 4 governs (Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 2 — Verified).

nodes.summary: Legend of power, control and instrument symbols (selector switches, relays, starters, field instruments, meters) plus a standard abbreviation list, including "E or (E) = existing device", MCP = main control panel, LCP = local control panel and MTS = manual transfer switch (E0.1 legend and abbreviations; plans_8 p.6) [Verified]. Notes 3–6: coordinate removal of existing equipment and phasing with the Owner to keep the facility operating, dispose of demo material the Owner does not want, conceal conduit in new walls and ceilings where possible, and hand over redline markups (routing, conductor counts, panel schedules, receptacle configurations) for record drawings (plans_8 p.6) [Verified]. Note 7: all conductors copper; terminations rated 60 °C at 100 A and below and 75 °C above 100 A, citing NEC Article 110-14C as printed (plans_8 p.6) [Verified]. nodes.summary: Existing 208Y/120V service being removed: OPALCO 45 kVA pad-mount utility transformer, CT enclosure and utility meter, 300 A SUSE-rated NEMA 3R service entrance breaker (SES), a 4-wire 3-pole automatic transfer switch (ATS), and a 30 kW / 37.5 kVA 208Y/120V diesel standby generator (GEN) with fuel tank, exhaust and louvers (one-line and demo plan; plans_8 p.7) [Verified-Visual]. Demo notes D1–D7: OPALCO replaces the 208Y/120V transformer with a 480Y/277V unit on the existing pad (downtime per specifications); remove the generator, fuel tank, exhaust and louvers and repair building openings per civil/architectural; remove the CT enclosure and meter after the new service is operational; remove the 300 A main breaker and the ATS; replace the 200 A feeder to Panel TPS; keep the existing grounding electrode system and bond new work to it; remove the obsolete meter base and wall raceway but keep the telephone junction box and service (plans_8 p.7) [Verified]. General note 1: the new 480Y/277V service with a new diesel generator re-feeds the existing 208 V equipment; general note 2: the Owner may keep any demo material and the contractor legally disposes of the rest (plans_8 p.7) [Verified]. Kept in service: Panel TPS in the Treatment Building (208Y/120V, 3-ph 4-W, 200 A) with its 100 A load center, and the Office Building distribution (400 A Square-D I-Line panel, 100 A switchboard, Lab panel, Panels SP and SH), labeled existing and outside the demo hatch (plans_8 p.7) [Verified for TPS; Office Building panels Verified-Visual].

nodes.summary: Area plan: influent pumps IP-1 to IP-4 (motors marked 3, 3, 5, 5) with floats and transducer and power/instrument handholes; WAS pumps WP-1, WP-2 and sludge pump SD-1 (marked 3) with local disconnects; dewatering skid control panel DW-1; three WAS solenoid valves; influent, plant 2, plant 3, plant drain and dewatering flow meters; methane and H2S sensors; exhaust fans EF-3 to EF-5; and one location holding the Influent Pump Station control panel, panel LP2 and the flow-meter transmitters (plan; plans_9 p.6) [Verified-Visual; IP-3/IP-4, EF-3 to EF-5, sensor and panel labels also in text]. Key notes 1–2: individual oversized conduits for every pump, float and transducer cable, duct-sealed at completion; flow meters are Endress+Hauser Promag W400 (Class I Div 2, EtherNet/IP, 316L electrodes, local display on the WAS meter, remote transmitters with submersible kits on vault meters) with two 316L grounding rings per tube — the drawing already shows the W400 that Add. 4 p.2 (26 80 00 ¶2.04 D) substitutes for the L400 (plans_9 p.6) [Verified]. Key notes 6–9: a dedicated 120 V GFCI receptacle and a 4–20 mA flow-pace signal from the PLC at four points (hypochlorite feed pump, polymer feed pump, influent sampler, effluent sampler; samplers Owner-furnished, contractor-installed); 120 VAC from LP2 and PLC control wiring to each of the three ventilation fans "in Treatment Building"; raceway to handholes with at least two 1-in spares from each power and control handhole stubbed and capped; influent pump motor disconnects on the building wall within sight of the wet well (plans_9 p.6) [Verified; numbering Verified-Visual]. Level control table (ft): redundant large lag on 19.00 (F1, timer), redundant large lead on 18.50 (F2), redundant small lag on 18.00 (F3), redundant small lead on 17.50 (F4), high level alarm 17.50 (transducer and float), large lag on 17.00, large lead on 16.00, small lag on 14.00, small lead on 12.00, pumps off 11.00, low level alarm and redundant off 10.50 — the table does not say which tags are the large pair; by E6.1 horsepower the 5 HP units IP-3/IP-4 are the large pumps (plans_9 p.7; plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual; large-pair assignment Inferred]. General notes number "4." twice (cosmetic) and repeat that handholes are required but not shown, with final locations coordinated with the Engineer (plans_9 p.7) [Verified].

nodes.summary: 2W Pump Station: two submersible pumps tagged P-2W-1 and P-2W-2 in equipment tag boxes (motors marked 5) with a factory float tree and two factory junction boxes, plus Hot Box #1 (1-in flow meter, isolation valve solenoid, GFEP, J-box, heat trace) and Hot Box #2 (heat trace); home runs P-2W, C-2W, S-2WFM and P-HB1, with P-HB2 and P-2WSV at the hot boxes (plan and hot box details; plans_9 p.8) [Verified-Visual; P-2WSV, S-2WFM, P-HB1, P-HB2 also in text]. Key notes 1–2: the pump system includes two factory junction boxes with strain-relief grips (one for motor cables, one for floats), power raceway to MCC buckets and control wiring to the PLC control panel, and a factory float tree with four floats — F1 (EQ# LSH-111) high level alarm and redundant valve close 22.00, F2 valve close 20.00, F3 valve open 19.00, F4 (EQ# LSL-111) low level alarm and pumps off 15.00 (plans_9 p.8) [Verified; float table Verified-Visual]. Key note 3: heat trace on all exposed piping — Raychem BTV self-regulating cable or equal on a dedicated 120 V 20 A GFEP circuit, NEMA 4X thermostat and end-of-line kit with indicator light (plans_9 p.8) [Verified]. Key notes 4–5: the 2W flow meter is a 1-in Endress+Hauser Promag W400 (24 VAC/DC, EtherNet/IP, local display, NEMA 4X) with two 316L grounding rings, matching Add. 4 p.2 (26 80 00 ¶2.04 D); solenoid and heat-trace power lands in a J-box in Hot Box #1 and extends to Hot Box #2 (plans_9 p.8) [Verified]. The pump tags differ from E6.1 (2W-P1, 2W-P2) and the meter signal run reads S-FM2W at the hot box but S-2WFM at the home run; Add. 4 p.3 (C1.3 item) re-orients "the 2W (Air Gap) Water Hot Box" for vehicle traffic — see Issues (plans_9 p.8; plans_10 p.2; Add. 4 p.3) [Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: E6.1 · Electrical One Line Diagram and Load Calculations
nodes.norm_label: e6.1 · electrical one line diagram and load calculations
nodes.summary: Service and distribution: OPALCO 225 kVA 480Y/277V pad-mount transformer → P-SEC → CT enclosure and utility meter → P-ATS → ATS (400 A service entrance, 4-wire 3-pole, NEMA 12, delayed open transition) with the 125 kW / 156 kVA standby diesel generator (sound-attenuated outdoor enclosure, sub-base fuel tank, 250/3, P-GEN) → P-MDP → MDP (480Y/277V, main lugs only, SPD) → 400/3 to the MCC and 125/3 to transformer TS (75 kVA 480–208Y/120V), which re-feeds the existing Office Building 400 A I-Line panel and, through its 200/3, Panel TPS (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual; tags also in text]. MCC (480 V 3-ph 4-W, Blower Building): 400/3 main, power monitor with (3) 400:5 CTs, SPD; 30/3 units for TCP-1 and TCP-2 (greyed, "future") and TCP-3; 60/3 for dewatering skid DW-1 and for the IPS panel; 60/2 to T2 (20 kVA 480–120/240V) and its load center; ten VFDs with line reactors — 2W-P1 and 2W-P2 (20/3, 5 HP), WP-1, WP-2 (swing) and SD-1 (15/3, 3 HP), all five with dV/dt reactors, BL-1 to BL-4 (35/3, 20 HP) and DB (20/3, 5 HP) (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. IPS Influent Pump Station control panel (480 V 3-ph 3-W, NEMA 4X SS): 60/3 main, contactor-and-overload starters for IP-1 and IP-2 (15/3, 3 HP) and IP-3 and IP-4 (20/3, 5 HP), and 30/2 to T3 (10 kVA 480–120/240V) and its load center; a local disconnect is drawn at each motor (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. Key notes: 1 the manufacturer sets VFD overcurrent protection ratings; 2 3% line-side reactors on all VFDs; 3 dV/dt load-side reactors on VFD motor runs over 50 ft; 4 outdoor control panel and disconnect enclosures Type 316 SS; 5 aeration blower disconnects are on the MCC within sight of the motors (plans_10 p.2) [Verified; numbering Verified-Visual]. Load calculations: 21 loads, 348.9 A connected, 355.7 A demand and 188.0 A on the generator (156 kVA at 480 V); generator factor 1 for TCP-1 to TCP-3, 2W-P1, IP-1, BL-1 to BL-3, DB and WP-1, 0 for the standby/swing units and DW-1, and 0.25 for LP-LAB (existing lab and treatment, 45 kVA), LP-1 (20 kVA) and LP-2 (10 kVA); the 355.7 A demand exceeds the E6.2 MDP total — see Issues (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual].

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.75 (plans_10 p.3); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 3 p.27 (set p.75); Wiki note E6.2 (Project_Wiki.md line 1025)
nodes.label: E6.2 · Electrical Panel Schedules
nodes.summary: Three panel schedules (MDP, LP1, LP2); the text layer carries only the titles, so every schedule entry is read from the page image (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. Panel MDP: 480Y/277V 3-ph 4-W, 400 A bus, 400 A main lugs only, surface mounted, 42,000 AIC; circuits 1-3-5 Blower Building MCC (400 A 3-pole, 60,000 VA per phase) and 2-4-6 transformer for existing building 480–208Y/120V (125 A 3-pole, 15,000 VA per phase); circuits 7–30 spaces; connected and demand 225.0 kVA, 270.6 A (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. Panel LP1 (MCC) repeats the E2.2 schedule without change: 120/240 V 1-ph 3-W, 100 A bus, 100 A main breaker, 10,000 AIC; receptacles, louver/HVAC control, EF-1, EF-2, UV1/UV2 power (30 A) and controllers, Main Control Panel, Blower Building lighting, generator heater and battery charger, Hot Box 1 and 2 GFEP, effluent sampler, hypochlorite feed pump; demand 17.3 kVA, 72.1 A (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. Panel LP2 (Influent Pump Station panel): 120/240 V 1-ph 3-W, 100 A bus, 60 A main breaker, 10,000 AIC; pump station control circuits, wall pack lighting, ventilation control panel, EF-3, EF-4, EF-5 (Treatment Building, 1,127 VA each), H2S and methane sensors, polymer feed pump and influent sampler receptacles, six spares; demand 7.8 kVA, 32.3 A; circuit numbers match the E4.1 callouts (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. Gaps against other sheets: the MDP total (225.0 kVA, 270.6 A) is below the E6.1 load-calculation demand (355.7 A), and no pole-light circuit appears on LP1 or LP2 although E6.3 feeds P-LT from a "lighting panel" — see Issues (plans_10 pp.2–4) [Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: E6.3 · Conduit and Conductor Schedules
nodes.summary: Power schedule: 40 named runs plus two unnamed 120 V UV controller circuits and an AC spare with pull string, each with voltage, conduit, conductor count and size, ground, from and to — e.g., P-SEC and P-ATS (2) 2-in 4 ea #3/0, P-GEN 3-in 4 #250 kcmil + #4 G, P-MCC (2) 2-in 4 ea #3/0 + #3 G, P-TSS (2) 2-in 4 ea #3/0 + #3 G (plans_10 p.4) [Verified-Visual; text layer carries titles only]. Control and signal schedule: 38 named 24 VDC runs plus a DC spare — C-ATS, C-GEN, C-2W, C-TCP3, C-DO1, C-DO2, C-MCP, C-INT, C-2WPT, C-SD1, C-DB, C-FME, C-UV, C-BL1 to C-BL4; S-LAB, S-LT-D, S-ICP, S-MCP, S-FLT1 to S-FLT4, S-LT-IP, S-DW1; factory coil and electrode cables S-FME, S-FMIN, S-FMPD, S-FMP2, S-FMP3; transmitter runs S-FMDW and S-FM2W; flow-pace runs S-FP1 to S-FP4 (plans_10 p.4) [Verified-Visual]. Closes batch 1 open items: P-TS3A (10 #14) feeds Train No.3 field devices and P-TS3B (4 #12) the Train No.3 pole light and receptacle; C-DO2 serves "DO transmitter No.2"; the Blower Building 2W transducer is called "2W pressure sensor" (plans_10 p.4) [Verified-Visual]. Disagreements with other sheets: P-IP1 to P-IP4 run "from MCC" while E6.1 feeds the influent pumps from the IPS panel; P-2W is one 2-in conduit with (2) 3-conductor cables to both 2W pumps while E6.1 shows P-2W-P1 and P-2W-P2; P-LT comes from an unnamed "lighting panel"; ID spellings differ (P-BL-1/P-BL1, P-SD-1/P-SD1, S-DW1/S-DW-1, S-FM2W/S-2WFM) — cosmetic (plans_10 p.4 vs plans_9 pp.3, 6, 8 and plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. Existing equipment is named differently from E0.2/E6.1: P-TSS ends at the "existing 208Y/120V 400A shop panel" and P-TPS starts at the "existing 208Y/120V shop SWBD" — both are the Office Building 400 A I-Line panel on the E6.1 one-line (plans_10 pp.2, 4) [Verified-Visual; identity Inferred].

nodes.label: E7.0 · Control System Overview
nodes.summary: Main PLC control panel: Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC and PanelView Plus operator interface on a network switch that links the MCC power monitor, the 2W and effluent flow meters and the VFDs in the MCC (typ of 10) (plans_10 p.5) [Verified-Visual; PLC, switch and meter labels also in text]. Influent Pump Station control panel: its own CompactLogix PLC (1768-ENBT) and network switch serving six flow meters — Train #1 (future), Train #2, Train #3, plant drain, influent and WAS (plans_10 p.5) [Verified]. Office: SCADA computer with alarm dialer on the existing telephone and internet service with a network switch (S-LAB); dewatering skid with its own network switch, operator interface and CompactLogix PLC (S-DW1); control handhole(s) on the S-ICP route; the cable legend distinguishes fiber optic and Cat 6 Ethernet (plans_10 p.5) [Verified-Visual]. General notes: the system integrator provides the detailed control panel design and documentation for a complete and operational system (only major components are specified), and all Ethernet-enabled equipment joins the control network with ports as required (plans_10 p.5) [Verified]. E7.0 calls the plant meters "Train #2/#3" and the dewatering meter "WAS"; E4.1 calls them plant 2, plant 3 and dewatering flow meters — the same meters by count and panel; the Train #1 meter appears only here (plans_10 p.5; plans_9 p.6) [Inferred].

nodes.summary: The drawing is titled "Main PLC and Influent Control Panel — Power Wiring Diagram (Typ)", so it serves both the main PLC panel and the Influent Pump Station panel; the operator interface and blower PTC relays are marked "main PLC only" and the 800 W panel heater "influent only" (plans_10 p.7) [Verified-Visual; title partly in text]. 120 VAC side: power from the lighting panel through a 20 A breaker and TVSS, 5 A branches for the door switch and enclosure light(s), a GFCI duplex programmer receptacle and a GFCI general receptacle, 1 A branches CBA4–8 for five motor PTC relay modules, the panel heater and six spares; final 120 VAC quantity and sizing per the system integrator (plans_10 p.7) [Verified-Visual]. 24 VDC side: 10 A 24 VDC power supply on a 20 A breaker, DC-UPS controller with a 12 VDC 26 AH battery assembly on a 30 A breaker and power-normal and alarm contacts to PLC inputs, 5 A breakers for the PLC power supply, operator interface and network switch, and 2 A fuses per card group for digital inputs, analog inputs, digital outputs, analog outputs and 24 VDC field power (plans_10 p.7) [Verified; fuse layout Verified-Visual]. Key note 1: the blower supplier provides a PTC relay module for installation in the main PLC panel; the system integrator installs it, provides a 120 V circuit to each and wires the overtemperature signal to the PLC to shut the blower motor down on high temperature (plans_10 p.7) [Verified].

nodes.summary: Five Allen-Bradley 1769-IQ16 16-point 24 VDC input cards (80 channels) with 74 field points drawn (plans_10 p.8) [Verified-Visual; counts taken from the image]. Card 1: DC UPS power normal and replace battery, main panel network switch status, ATS utility power normal and emergency position, generator running and alarm, UV1 and UV2 controller status, and digester blower hand, auto, VFD running and VFD fault; cards 2–3: aeration blowers 1–4 hand, auto, VFD running and VFD fault, high motor temperature (key note 1, blower supplier PTC relay) and high enclosure temperature for the digester blower and aeration blower 1–4 enclosures, and the Blower Building intrusion door switch and smoke detector (plans_10 p.8) [Verified-Visual; labels also in text]. Card 4: Treatment Cell 1 and Cell 2 control panels (greyed, "FUTURE") and the Treatment Cell 3 control panel, each running, alarm and shutdown; 2W pump station floats F1–F4; WAS pump 1. Card 5: WAS pump 2, sludge pump, and 2W pumps 1 and 2, each hand, auto, VFD running and VFD fault (plans_10 p.8) [Verified-Visual]. Numbering errors: card 4 carries 17 points on 16 channels (DI14 used twice), card 5 numbers both 2W pumps DI13, DI14, DI14, DI15, and fuse label FU-DI3 repeats on cards 3 and 5; the 74 points fit the 80 channels if renumbered — see Issues (plans_10 p.8) [Verified-Visual; fit Inferred by count].

nodes.summary: One Allen-Bradley 1769-OB16 16-point 24 VDC output card driving interposing relays CR0–CR15 (plans_11 p.1) [Verified-Visual; card and relay labels also in text]. Outputs 0–9 are "call to run" contacts into the MCC VFD control circuits: aeration blowers 1–4 (outputs 0–3), digester blower (4), WAS pumps 1 and 2 (5–6), sludge pump (7), and 2W pumps 1 and 2 (8–9) (plans_11 p.1) [Verified-Visual]. Output 10 switches 120 V to the 2W solenoid valve "call to open" at Hot Box #1; outputs 11–15 are spares, so 11 of 16 are used (plans_11 p.1) [Verified-Visual]. The text layer sets "CR10 … 2W PUMP #1 … OUT 10" and "CR12 2W SOLENOID VALVE … OUT 12" side by side; the image shows OUT 8 for 2W pump #1 and OUT 10 for the solenoid, and the assignments here follow the image (workflow log) (plans_11 p.1) [Verified-Visual].

nodes.norm_label: e8.1 · influent pump station control panel elevations
nodes.summary: Exterior: NEMA 4X Type 316 stainless steel enclosure with drip shield, sized to hold all equipment, on a concrete equipment pad "per civil specifications"; key note 1 calls for local control of the influent pumps, seal-fail and overtemperature wiring and instrumentation, with controls on an internal swing-out door behind a lockable outer door (plans_11 p.5) [Verified; enclosure label Verified-Visual]. Swing-out door: influent wet well level display; for each of pumps 1–4 a hand-off-auto switch and run, fail, seal-fail and overtemperature lights with reset; four float-activated lights with float test buttons (plans_11 p.5) [Verified-Visual; labels also in text]. Backpanel: main 480 V disconnect; panel LP2 with its transformer and overcurrent protection; area light hand-off-auto and GFCI receptacle; panel heater and thermostat; power distribution block and phase monitor; pump circuit breakers and full-voltage NEMA starters for influent pumps 1–4; field terminals for motor connections; network switch and PLC rack; DC power supply and UPS; interposing relays; seal-fail relays; intrinsically safe area with barriers for the floats and level transducer (plans_11 p.5) [Verified]. Key notes 2–4: flow meter transmitters for influent, Cell 1 (future space), Cell 2, Cell 3 and plant drain, with coil and electrode cables from the meter vaults; seal-fail and overtemperature relays (Mini-CAS or equal) furnished by the pump manufacturer and coordinated by the system integrator; field conduits not shown — route all raceway shown on the plans to the influent control panel (plans_11 p.5) [Verified]. The backpanel takes "power from MCC" and holds the pump starters, agreeing with E6.1 rather than E6.3 on the influent pump feeders; the WAS/dewatering meter is not in the transmitter list, consistent with its local display (E4.1 key note 2) — see Issues (plans_11 p.5; plans_10 pp.2, 4; plans_9 p.6) [Verified-Visual; WAS reading Inferred].

nodes.summary: Schematic power wiring: 480 V 3-phase into a power distribution block with a surge suppressor, a phase-fail relay and control transformer CPT1 (120 VAC control power), then a breaker, motor starter and overload for each of pumps 1–4 (plans_11 p.6) [Verified-Visual; labels also in text]. Pump data as printed: pump no.1 and no.2 "XP" 3 HP, 4.8 FLA; pump no.3 and no.4 "XP" 5 HP, 7.6 FLA — matching the E6.1 horsepower for IP-1 to IP-4 (plans_11 p.6; plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. Pump control wiring, typical for each of 4 pumps: hand-off-auto; in auto the starter runs on a PLC contact or, in parallel, the high-float contact; the starter coil is interlocked by the overtemperature relay, the phase-fail relay and the overload; lights for pump running, overtemperature, seal fail and overload (plans_11 p.6) [Verified-Visual]. Seal-fail/overtemperature relay per pump, wired to the pump housing sensors (T1, T2) with a reset, driving relays CROT and CRSF (plans_11 p.6) [Verified-Visual; relay labels also in text]. General note 1: the system integrator provides the detailed panel design; only major components are specified (plans_11 p.6) [Verified].

nodes.summary: Two Allen-Bradley 1769-IQ16 16-point input cards, all 32 channels used: influent pumps 1–4 (hand, auto, running, fault, seal fail, overtemperature — six each), wet well floats F1–F4 through relays ISR-F1B to ISR-F4B, ventilation fans 1–3 "called to run" from the ventilation control panel, and phase fail (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual]. General note 2 calls for added I/O cards to give at least 20% spare inputs, not shown; with 32 of 32 inputs used that means at least 7 more inputs, a third card (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual; card count Inferred by arithmetic]. Each pump input block is labeled "INFLUENT PUMP n: MCC", and pump 2 shows "VFD FAULT" with no "auto selected" input, unlike pumps 1, 3 and 4 — see Issues (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual]. High-level float control circuit (hardwired backup): each wet well high-level float passes an intrinsic safety barrier (relays ISR-FnA/FnB), lights a "high float activated" panel light, has a test button, and "starts pump n" through relay CRHn with a time-off-delay relay TDRn, 0–60 s; key note 1 sets true-off delay, field-adjusted to wet well pump-down rate (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual; key note Verified]. Float n is wired to pump n (F1 to 3 HP pump 1), while the E4.2 level table assigns F1 and F2 to the large pumps — see Issues (plans_11 p.7; plans_9 p.7) [Verified-Visual; large-pump reading Inferred from horsepower].

nodes.summary: Typical VFD unit: lockable circuit breaker disconnect, power distribution block, 480/120 V 350 VA control transformer, 3% line reactor, Allen-Bradley PowerFlex 753 with Ethernet communication module, door-mounted HIM on RS485, dV/dt filter for motor runs over 50 ft, motor terminal block (plans_12 p.4) [Verified-Visual; PowerFlex 753 also in text]. Control: hand-off-auto with hand and auto status to the PLC panel; PLC relay "call to run" through the motor overtemperature contact to relay CR1; a 10 kΩ hand speed potentiometer; running (CR3) and fault (CR4) contacts to the PLC with push-to-test running and fault lights; MCC cooling fan(s) on a thermostat and the blower enclosure fan on the unit control power (plans_12 p.4) [Verified-Visual]. Key note 1: provide a 120 V blower fan circuit from each MCC unit for each blower; basis of design 0.21 HP and 1.51 A per fan, confirmed with the manufacturer during submittals (plans_12 p.4) [Verified]. Key note 2: in hand, speed comes from the potentiometer on the MCC door or field panel; in auto, speed command and feedback go direct to the PLC over Ethernet, and analog speed hardwiring is not required. Key note 3: wire the motor thermal contact to each VFD where available; jumper the terminals when the motor has none (plans_12 p.4) [Verified].

nodes.summary: Ventilation control panel: NEMA 4X stainless steel enclosure; door carries H2S alarm and methane alarm lights, run lights and OFF/ON switches for ventilation fans 1–3, and an alarm horn (plans_12 p.5) [Verified-Visual]. nodes.summary: Grounding system detail (service equipment ground bus bonded to metallic cold-water piping and to foundation rebar at least once; contractor provides all grounding and bonding per NEC 250) and ground rod detail (precast grounding well, ground loop copper wire, rod) (plans_12 p.6) [Verified-Visual; detail text not in the text layer]. Electrical handhole detail: 3 ft-8 in x 2 ft-8 in precast vault, basis of design Oldcastle Precast #233-LA (vault #233-BL, cover #23-2436P) or equal, upsized where the NEC requires; galvanized diamond-plate traffic cover with locking latch, grounded per NEC; 6 in sump over compacted drainage rock (coordinate with civil); 18 x 18 in knockouts each end; 8 ft copper-clad ground rod; covers labeled "ELECTRIC" or "SIGNAL" (plans_12 p.6) [Verified]. Secondary and feeder raceway detail: burial 24 in for feeders and 36 in for secondary and primary, 18 in minimum trench width, "ELECTRICAL" warning tape 12 in below grade, backfill per civil; raceway notes require 12 in separation from water utilities, 2 in between conduits and to the trench wall, and sand bedding 3 in below and above the conduit (plans_12 p.6) [Verified-Visual]. Equipment rack detail (stainless Unistrut on posts set in concrete); intrinsically safe relay connection detail (floats and submersible transducer on factory cables to explosion-proof junction boxes with seal-off fittings in a handhole outside the wet well, then to the intrinsically safe area in the control panels); wet well instrumentation detail (floats and transducer on stainless hooks with Kellems grips, watertight core-drilled riser penetrations) (plans_12 p.6) [Verified]. The wet well detail labels a "LOW LEVEL FLOAT (TYP)", while E4.2 and E8.3 show four high-level floats and no low-level float — see Issues (plans_12 p.6; plans_9 p.7; plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: G0.3 · Notes & Specifications
nodes.summary: The Contractor must not interrupt District operations, must verify locations and depths of existing utilities (shown for information only), must report dimension discrepancies to the Engineer, and must repair damage to existing improvements within 48 hours (General Notes 1, 3–6; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified). Trenches and excavations must meet federal OSHA requirements, and trench shoring design and installation are the Contractor's full responsibility (General Note 7; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified). A 1-week notice to the District is required before any utility service disruption, and the Contractor must provide temporary equipment (power generator, pumps, piping) and an approved plan for all WWTP disruptions; the note cites 'Section 01 11 00', whose body number is 01 11 10 (General Note 10; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified; alias already flagged, 02 conflict 1). The Operation Plan makes the Contractor responsible for sequencing so the existing WWTP is not interrupted and for all temporary bypass pumping, piping, holding tanks and storage (Operation Plan 1–3; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified). Survey monuments disturbed by construction need WA DNR permits under WAC 332-120 and replacement by a registered land surveyor at Contractor cost; earthwork, concrete and asphalt repair are to be prioritized in dry-weather months; County inspections (footings, concrete structures, electrical, final) and S1.1 special inspections need 24-hour notice to Owner and Engineer (Schedule, Survey Monumentation and Construction Inspections notes; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified).

nodes.label: G0.5 · Process Schematic
nodes.summary: 8" STEP influent and an influent sample sump feed the Influent Pump Station, which pumps through a 6" influent flow meter to the flow splitter; the splitter feeds Treatment Cell #1 (Train #1) on INF1, Treatment Cell #2 (Train #2) through an 8" Train #2 flow meter on INF2, and New Treatment Cell #3 (Train #3) through an 8" Train #3 flow meter on INF3, with a fourth outlet marked FUTURE. Secondary effluent SE1–SE3 passes an 8" effluent flow meter into UV Channels #1 and #2, then 10" final effluent runs to SSMH *1288 and the 12" outfall; a 4" UV chamber drain is shown. WAS1–WAS3 go to a WAS pump and the aerobic digester above the UV chamber; a digested sludge pump with a flow meter feeds the rotary fan press and the existing screw press (drawn gray), and the 4" pressate drain returns through a 4" plant drain flow meter to the pump station. Train #3 shows Anoxic 1, Anoxic 2, Aeration 1, Aeration 2 and a clarifier, with ML recycle airlift pumps, a RAS airlift pump, and a carbon addition point into Anoxic 2. Legend: isolation valve, flow direction, flow meter (FM), airlift pump.

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.6 (plans_1 p.6); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 1 p.6 (set p.6); Wiki note G0.6 (Project_Wiki.md line 354)
nodes.label: G0.6 · Hydraulic Profile
nodes.summary: The liquid profile runs from the proposed influent sampling sump (FG 23.65) and the proposed influent & plant drain pump station (8" influent from the STEP collection system, IE 19.50; FG 23.30) through the plant influent flow meter to the proposed 3-way splitter box (HWL 28.0 at 0.77 MGD; bottom elev 26.00). Existing Trains #1 and #2 run at HWL 23.13 (0.257 MGD), NWL 23.09 (0.063 MGD), static 23.05; proposed Train #3 runs at HWL 25.38, NWL 25.34, static 25.30, top of concrete 26.80, with proposed Train #2 and Train #3 flow meters on the inlets. The proposed effluent flow meter feeds proposed UV disinfection channels #1 and #2 (HWL 21.49 at 0.50 MGD per channel; NWL 19.69 at 0.22 MGD per channel), then existing SSMH *1288 (rim 22.89) and 10" and 8" to the 12" outfall; the 100-year flood elevation is 13', and a proposed effluent sample sump is labeled. The solids profile shows proposed WAS pump equipment (pump rate 20–30 gpm), the proposed aerobic digester with a supernatant telescoping valve (TOC 26.80; supernatant to the plant drain P.S.), proposed sludge pump equipment (20–30 gpm), proposed rotary fan press dewatering equipment and the existing screw press, with filtrate to the plant drain P.S. and solids hauled off site.

nodes.citation: 01 Sheet Index rev2, set p.7 (plans_1 p.7); Plan_Set_Parts.md Part 1 p.7 (set p.7); Wiki note G0.7 (Project_Wiki.md line 364)
nodes.label: G0.7 · Design Criteria
nodes.summary: Start-up design (after Phase I) is ADF 0.10, MMF 0.12, max day 0.30 and peak hour 0.49 MGD; build-out (year 2040, after Phase II — phase numerals read from the image, Verified-Visual) is 0.19, 0.22, 0.46 and 0.77 MGD. The Influent Pump Station has 2 small submersible pumps (120–220 gpm each) and 2 large (320–500 gpm each), firm capacity 535 gpm (0.77 MGD) with one small and one large out of service; electromagnetic flow meters are influent 6" (0–880 gpm), Train #2 and Train #3 8" (0–470 gpm each), effluent 8" (0–940 gpm), plant drain 4" (0–200 gpm) and 2W water 1" (0–25 gpm). Train 3 has one 5 HP submersible mixer in each anoxic zone (#1 15,686 gal, #2 8,789 gal), aeration zone #1 (29,793 gal, 8 diffusers, 192 scfm) and zone #2 (9,889 gal, 2 diffusers, 48 scfm) with "medium bubble" aeration mixing, a RAS airlift (15 scfm, 3", 51 gpm) and a nitrate recycle airlift (61 scfm, 6", 203 gpm), for 316 scfm total at 9.2 psig; clarifiers are 3 units, 18 ft, SWD 13.25' (cells 1–2) and 15.50' (cell 3). UV has 2 lamps per module, 8 modules per channel and 2 channels at 0.5 MGD each, design dose printed "30,000 MJ/CM2" and UVT 50% or greater; the aerobic digester is 15,000 gal with coarse bubble aeration (6 diffusers × 20 cfm) and manual T-valve decant control. WAS and digester pumps are each 1 duty + 1 standby (swing) hose (peristaltic) pumps, 0–40 gpm; one rotary fan press takes 12 gpm at 2% or 20 gpm at 0.5% solids and makes 12–16% cake (up to 1,000 wet / 120 dry lb/hr); 2W water pumps are 1 duty + 1 standby submersible, 20–80 gpm on VFD control.

nodes.summary: Design basis is the 2018 IBC, Risk Category III, 100 psf floor live load, 25 psf ground and flat-roof snow (Ct 1.1, Ce 1.1, Is 1.1), 105 mph ultimate wind (Exposure C), and seismic Site Class D (default), SDC D, Ie 1.25, SDS 0.79g, SD1 0.51g [plans_7 p.8, S1.1 General Notes 1–6 — Verified-Visual]. Foundations use 2,500 psf allowable bearing (×1.33 for wind or seismic), a minimum 1'-6" frost cover, and the GeoEngineers report dated September 7, 2021 (clouded, revision 2) for subgrade, backfill and compaction [plans_7 p.8, Foundations & Subgrade 1, 2, 8 — Verified-Visual; report-date conflict already flagged in 02 Unresolved spec items #2 and the 03 Merge flag — cited, not re-raised]. The concrete material schedule sets 4,500 psi and 0.45 max w/cm for three groups: Blower Building slab-on-grade, grade beams and misc. equipment pads (3/4" aggregate, 6% air, 30% min fly ash/slag); hydraulic structures (1" aggregate, air per notes, 20%); and the "Drain Pump Station Lid" (3/4", 5%, 20%) [plans_7 p.8, Reinforced Concrete 2 — Verified-Visual]. Minimum structural shop drawings are concrete reinforcing (including wall elevations), mix designs, a slab-on-grade jointing plan and structural steel; deferred submittals, sealed by a Washington PE, are metal stairs & landings and the pre-engineered metal building for the Blower Building [plans_7 p.8, Submittals 4–5 — Verified-Visual]. Structural steel follows AISC 303-16 with A992 W/WT, A500 Gr B HSS, A53 Gr B pipe, A325 bolts, F1554 Gr 36 anchor rods, A36 misc. steel and E70XX welds, exterior steel hot-dip galvanized; a structural special inspection schedule covers steel, concrete, post-installed anchors, and soils and foundations [plans_7 p.8, Structural Steel 1–4 and Special Inspection schedule — Verified-Visual].

nodes.summary: Train 3 is a circular cast-in-place tank: a 12" concrete wall on a 12" mat slab foundation with a raised center pedestal [plans_8 p.1, S2.1 Detail 1 — Verified-Visual]. Wall reinforcing is #5 horizontal at 12" o.c. each face (Grade 75 bars, laps staggered per Detail 5) and #5 vertical at 12" o.c. each face with 3" clear, plus (2) #4 horizontal at the top [plans_8 p.1, Detail 4 — Verified-Visual]. Slab reinforcing is continuous #5 at 12" o.c. with #5 radial bars at 12" o.c. at the outer edge (top shown, bottom similar; 2" clear top, 3" clear bottom), the pedestal has #5 radial bars at 16" o.c., and the slab center adds #5 × 8'-0" top and bottom bars with radial bars ending at 3'-0" and 1'-0" diameter rings [plans_8 p.1, Details 1–3 — Verified-Visual]. Detail 4 requires a hydrophilic waterstop (submit for approval), a grout surface per spec, and subgrade preparation per the structural notes and geotech report, and shows "guardrail, mechanical equipment, and ladders per civil" [plans_8 p.1, Detail 4 — Verified-Visual]. Horizontal laps may align vertically only at every third bar or more, with lap length per 3/S4.1 [plans_8 p.1, Detail 5 — Verified-Visual]; the S4.1 table covers Grade 60 uncoated bars only while these horizontal bars are Grade 75 [plans_8 p.5; Add. 4 p.10, S4.1 Detail 3 Note 1 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved: need Grade 75 lap lengths — Issues, Conflicts #2].

nodes.summary: The foundation plan shows two cast-in-place basins on 12" mat slab foundations — a UV basin with 8" concrete walls and a digester with 12" concrete walls — with an HDG W8×18 beam spanning the digester, connected to the wall at each end per Detail 7 [plans_8 p.2, S2.2 Detail 1 — Verified-Visual]. Mat slab reinforcing is called out twice as "typical for mat slabs this plan," once as #6 @ 10" o.c. T&B and once as #6 @ 12" o.c. T&B, and reinforcing at penetrations follows 6/S4.1 and 7/S4.1 [plans_8 p.2, Detail 1 — Verified-Visual; spacing — Unresolved: need engineer clarification, Issues, Conflicts #1]. Sections A-A, B-B and C-C show #5 and #6 wall bars at 10"–12" o.c. (each face in the 12" walls, centered in the 8" walls) hooked 3" clear from bottom, a hydrophilic waterstop at all construction joints (submit for approval), an unreinforced sloped concrete topping per civil, subgrade preparation per the structural notes and geotech report, and "guardrail & ladders per civil" [plans_8 p.2, Details 2–4 — Verified-Visual]. Inside the UV basin, 8" concrete walls support the equipment in 4 places (#5 @ 12" o.c. each way, vertical bars drilled and epoxied to the slab), with 3" mechanical equipment pads reinforced per civil at each end of the equipment [plans_8 p.2, Detail 3 — Verified-Visual]. Aluminum solid plank grating per the specifications (submit for approval; attachment by manufacturer) bears on a continuous HDG 1/4" steel edge angle at wall tops (Detail 5) and a continuous HDG L3×3×1/4 with 5/8" drilled-and-epoxied anchors at 24" o.c. at wall faces (Detail 6); Detail 7 connects the HDG beam to the wall with HDG L4×4×3/8 angles, 3/4" A307 bolts and 5/8" epoxy anchors [plans_8 p.2, Details 5–7 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.summary: The drain pump station lid is a 16"-thick cast-in-place concrete lid over an 8' min., 96" I.D. precast wet well (lid diameter to match the wet well O.D.), designed for H-20 truck loading, with two hatches per civil at 2'-6" × 4'-0" rough openings and a center beam between them [plans_8 p.4, S2.4 Detail 1 and Notes 1–6 — Verified-Visual]. Lid bars are placed in a set order (E/W bottom, N/S bottom, N/S top, E/W top) with 1-1/2" clear, the center beam has (2) #8 top and bottom continuous with #4 closed ties @ 3" o.c. max., and the lid keys into the precast wall with joints to be "seal AA at joints per civil" [plans_8 p.4, Details 1–3 — Verified-Visual]. Add. 4 requires the exterior of all precast concrete wet well and vault joints to be sealed with CANUSA-CPS WrapidSeal (manhole encapsulation system) or approved equal, installed per the manufacturer [Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 2 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The generator sits on a 6" slab-on-grade (#4 @ 18" o.c. each way, mid-depth) with a thickened edge about 1'-6" min. deep and (2) #4 continuous; the generator itself is "per civil, attachment by others" and is not identified as permanent or temporary [plans_8 p.4, Detail 4 — Verified-Visual; identity — Unresolved, Issues, Missing information #5]. The flow splitter sits on a new concrete pad on the existing equipment slab-on-grade, reinforced #4 @ 12" o.c. each way top and bottom with #4 hooked dowels @ 24" o.c. drilled and epoxied around the perimeter and a roughened joint; flow splitter per civil, pad per mech and civil, attachment by others [plans_8 p.4, Detail 5 — Verified-Visual].

Add. 4 adds Detail 8, a trench in the existing slab for sub-floor pipe: saw-cut the existing slab (24" max.), encase the new pipe in CDF (1,000 psi min.), infill to match the existing slab thickness with #4 dowels @ 18" o.c. alternating sides, drilled and epoxied with 4" min. embedment, and sleeve per 6/S2.3 without coring through rebar where pipe passes under or through an existing footing [Add. 4 p.10, Detail 8 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 governs]. nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 54), main spec pp.16–20; Wiki note 00 24 13 (Project_Wiki.md line 1291)
nodes.label: 00 24 13 · Scopes of Bids
nodes.status: Main spec pp.16–20 · Bid item scopes → 04_Bid_Item_Spine.md
nodes.summary: Describes where costs belong for each bid item in 00 41 00; each item is furnished, installed and tested, complete and in full operation before Owner acceptance (p.16; Verified). Item 1 WWTP Upgrade (LS) is paid per the approved Schedule of Values and covers all work in the Contract Documents; Items 2–5 cover trench safety (per WSDOT and OSHA — Unresolved: external reference, not staged), 12 bollards at Owner-chosen locations, SWPPP preparation with transfer of the NPDES construction stormwater permit, and SWPPP maintenance (¶1–5, pp.16–17; Verified except as tagged). Item 6 Electrical covers all E sheets and Division 26 (breakdowns in 26 05 00 and 26 80 00), and Item 7 Minor Changes covers changes of $100,000 or less that do not change Contract Time (¶6–7, p.17; Verified). Items 8–16 are unit-price contingencies for HMA, structural concrete, over-excavation and aggregates, and Item 17 is force-account SCADA/PLC programming; aggregate specs and force account defer to WSDOT 9-03 and 1-09.6 (¶8–17, pp.17–20; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Bid Alternates 1 and 2 (Items 18, 19) add Type 316 stainless steel for Train 3 in-basin steel components above water (to 1 ft below) or throughout, excluding FRP weirs and covers, per 46 53 00 (¶18–19, p.20; Verified); the Item 18 conflict with Add. 4 is flagged in 02/03/04 (cited, not re-raised).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 55), main spec pp.21–22; Wiki note 00 31 13 (Project_Wiki.md line 1307)
nodes.label: 00 31 13 · Preliminary Project Phase
nodes.summary: The phasing plan is for planning only and does not dictate means and methods (p.21; Verified). San Juan County building permit applications were submitted Nov 2021 with approvals June 2022; bid phase: advertise Jan 4, pre-bid Jan 18, open bids Feb 8, award Feb 15, preconstruction meeting Mar 15, 2023 (p.21; Verified). Construction starts with submittals after award (long-lead items first) and March 2023 mobilization, a temporary bypass pipe per the Plan of Interim Operation (April 2023), then Blower Building, digester, UV disinfection chamber, sludge pumps, yard piping, vaults and electrical (April 2023), the 2W air gap water system (May 2023), influent pump station (June 2023) and Train 3 (August 2023) (¶A.1–10, p.21; Verified). A temporary 480V generator is rented from Sept 25, 2023 until the permanent 480V generator is installed, tested and on line in April 2024, and the new 480V service, MCC and PLC panel complete Oct 4, 2023 (¶A.11–12, p.21; ¶A.21, p.22; Verified). Milestones: major piping Nov 1, 2023; dewatering system Feb 9, 2024; Train 3 complete July 8, 2024 then seeded with 10,000 gal of activated sludge July 8–12; Substantial Completion July 26, 2024; Final Completion Oct 16, 2024 (¶A.18–27, p.22; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 56), main spec pp.23–28; Wiki note 00 41 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1323)
nodes.label: 00 41 00 · Bid Proposal
nodes.status: Main spec pp.23–28 · Addendum 4: Bid Item #18 cited — Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 5 (conflict) · Bid items and alternates → 04_Bid_Item_Spine.md. Bid Item #18 (p.25) conflicts with Add. 4 — Unresolved; flag: Merge exception report
nodes.summary: The form carries Base Bid Item 1 WWTP Upgrade (LS), unit-quantity Items 2–7, extra-work Items 8–17, Bid Alternate 1 (Item 18) and Bid Alternate 2 (Item 19), then 8.3% sales tax (Eastsound Sewer and Water District, San Juan County) and total bid (pp.23–25; Verified). The Owner pre-enters $100,000.00 for Item 7 Minor Changes (EST) and $100,000.00 for Item 17 Extra SCADA/PLC Programmer Services (FA) (pp.23–24; Verified). Base Bid Item 1 is based on the named manufacturers — Flygt submersible pumps, Smith and Loveless biological treatment, Fournier or Prime Solutions rotary fan press, Trojan UV, and Cummins/Kohler/Caterpillar/Generac generators — with Equipment Alternates A–E as lump-sum deductions; there is no pre-bid approval review and the bidder carries all redesign cost (pp.26–27; Verified). Mobilization is paid per WSDOT 1-09.7 (Unresolved: external reference, not staged); completion time points to "Supplementary Condition 15 – Completion Date", liquidated damages are per the General Conditions per calendar day, and the Owner may accept or reject bid prices within 60 days (p.27; Verified — the 60 days vs 45 days in 00 21 13 is Issues 1.4). Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 5 uses "Bid Item #18" for the temporary back-up generator while this form lists Item 18 as Train 3 stainless steel above water (p.25): Add. 4 governs the temporary generator requirements; the item number stays Unresolved per the existing flag (cited, not re-raised).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 67), main spec pp.41–65; Wiki note 00 53 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1483)
nodes.label: 00 53 00 · WPCRF Inserts
nodes.summary: Ecology WPCRF clauses are incorporated and take precedence in any conflict within the contract (p.41; Verified) — not placed in the 00 73 00 SC 2 order (Issues 2.7). Required with the bid: Certification of Nonsegregated Facilities (Attachment 3), EPA DBE forms 6100-4 and 6100-3 (one per DBE sub; forms on the Ecology website), and the complete Bidders List (p.41; Verified); pp.45–46 then allow the DBE forms and the Bidders List "as part of the bid, or within one hour" after bid time (Verified) — timing conflicts inside this section and with 00 43 93 and 01 33 00 (Issues 1.6). Site and records clauses: safe access for Ecology and EPA, separate auditable project records kept 3 years after final audit, no discharge to state waters without Ecology approval, a funding-recognition sign visible from nearby roadways for the life of the project with Department logos, and the Inadvertent Discovery Plan kept on site with work stopped on any discovery (pp.41–42; Verified). American Iron and Steel applies to treatment works: iron and steel products (pipe and fittings, castings, hydrants, tanks, flanges, restraints, valves, structural steel, reinforced precast, construction materials) must be US-produced unless waived, with certification on request and damages for non-compliance (pp.42–43; Verified). Davis-Bacon, debarment, DBE six good faith efforts, 30-day sub payment, EEO (EO 11246) and segregated-facilities clauses follow, with Attachment 1 (DB terms, pp.53–61), Attachment 2 (DB wage determination — an unfilled placeholder, p.62; Issues 2.4), Attachment 3 (p.64) and Attachment 4 notice to labor unions (p.65) (pp.43–65; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 72), main spec pp.88–121; Wiki note 00 73 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1563)
nodes.label: 00 73 00 · Supplementary Conditions
nodes.summary: Thirty-five Supplemental Conditions modify the WSDOT Standard Specifications (2022 Ed.), which serve as the base conditions (Unresolved: external reference, not staged); precedence runs Change Orders, Contract Form, Addenda, permits, Drawings, Supplemental Conditions, Technical Specifications, District standards, WSDOT drawings, WSDOT specs (SC 1–2, 5, pp.88–89; Verified); the 00 53 00 and 00 54 00 funding inserts are not placed in that order (Issues 2.7). The Contractor stakes the work, picks up the District Land Disturbance permit and San Juan County Building Permit #21-0385 (stated as still in process), gives 48-hour utility and connection notices, works 7AM–5PM Mon–Fri with $150/hr inspection charge past 40 hr/week, and self-performs at least 50% of the contract price (SC 7–14, pp.89–91; Verified; permit status conflicts with 00 31 13 — Issues 1.9). SC 15 sets completion by Oct. 16, 2024 within 360 working days on site; SC 16 requires the CPM schedule at the pre-construction meeting and the Schedule of Values within 10 working days of NTP; SC 17 holds 5% retainage; SC 18 sets liquidated damages per working day as LD = 0.15C/T per WSDOT 1-08.9 (pp.91–92; Verified; WSDOT part Unresolved: external reference, not staged; basis conflicts with 00 41 00 — Issues 1.8). SC 19 defines Substantial Completion as the new facility in beneficial use (influent pump station, flow splitter, Train 3, digester, dewatering, blower building, UV, yard piping, electrical, instruments, controls, backup generator, SCADA/PLC programming) and Final Completion as including removal of temporary pump/process equipment, site work, paving, performance testing and cleanup (p.92; Verified). Red-line record drawings before 90% payment, temporary barriers at all hazards, insurance ($1M/$2M bodily injury, $1M property damage, builders risk equal to the bid, Owner and Engineer additional insured), one-year guarantee (start date conflicts — Issues 1.11), and funding clauses follow (SC 20–35, pp.92–97; Verified); pp.98–121 repeat the 00 53 00 Ecology insert word for word (Issues 1.13).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 74), main spec pp.123–125; Wiki note 01 11 10 (Project_Wiki.md line 1579)
nodes.label: 01 11 10 · Summary of Work
nodes.status: Main spec pp.123–125 · Body number governs; alias 01 11 00 accepted (decision E); stays Unresolved — see conflict log
nodes.summary: The work is all labor, equipment and materials for the WWTP improvements and miscellaneous site improvements — in general, expansion of the existing plant — including demolition, shoring, bracing, sheeting, cribbing, falsework, pumping, dewatering, drainage and forms, except items pre-purchased or supplied by the Owner; 00 24 13 holds the detailed scope (¶1.01, p.123; Verified). No Owner-furnished items are listed in this section (p.123; Verified absence). Sequence is the Contractor's option, with the preliminary phasing in 00 31 13, Owner approval of stockpile areas, and staging coordinated with the District (¶1.03, ¶1.05, pp.123–124; Verified). Suppliers are responsible for complete, compatible installations including missing connections; design is based on the first-named manufacturer and substitutes carry their own redesign cost; gravity drainage has right-of-way over mechanical and electrical, and electrical over landscaping (¶1.04, p.124; Verified). Excavation follows RCW 19.122 with 811 notice 48 hours ahead and Engineer notice 48 hours before starting, plus access, storage and restoration duties (¶1.06–1.07, p.125; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 75), main spec pp.126–128; Wiki note 01 31 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1595)
nodes.label: 01 31 00 · Project Coordination
nodes.summary: Project meetings coordinate the work, resolve conflicts, review progress and quality, and keep the work on schedule; attendees must have authority to act (¶1.01, p.126; Verified). Related sections include "00 25 13 Pre-Bid Conference", which is not in the 02 index (Issues 2.5), and "01 11 00", the accepted alias of 01 11 10 (¶1.02, p.126). The pre-construction meeting follows the Notice to Proceed per the General Conditions time frame and covers schedule, phasing, liquidated damages, Owner-furnished materials status, staking, labor standards, rights-of-way and placement of project signs and posters (¶1.03, pp.126–127; Verified; timing conflicts with SC 13 — Issues 1.10). The Owner runs weekly progress meetings near the site with Engineer minutes within a week (¶1.04, p.127; Verified). A preliminary CPM schedule is due within 10 days of Contract Award, updated monthly with the pay estimate and kept at the Contractor's field office (¶1.05, pp.127–128; Verified; due date conflicts — Issues 1.12).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 76), main spec pp.129–132; Wiki note 01 33 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1611)
nodes.label: 01 33 00 · Submittal Procedures
nodes.summary: Gives general submittal procedures and a non-exhaustive checklist; item-specific requirements sit in the individual sections (¶1.01, ¶1.03, p.129; Verified). The checklist's bid-phase entries cite sections and attachments that do not exist in the project manual — 00 43 36, 00 22 13, 00 45 14, and DBE forms as "Attachments 6 and 7" of 00 73 00 — and move Contractor Qualifications to 24 hours after opening (¶1.03.A–C, p.129; Issues 1.14, 2.2, 2.5). Before the Agreement: bonds, insurance certificates, prevailing wage filings; 10 days after execution: construction schedule, substitution requests, Schedule of Values; monthly: pay application and updated schedule; certified payroll; 14 days before any WWTP shutdown: a bypass pumping and emergency response plan; closeout: affidavits, record drawings (¶1.03.D–J, pp.129–130; Verified). Submittals are PDF with a transmittal, stamped by the Contractor, with an approved-submittal file kept on site; samples in pairs, product certificates in triplicate, test reports 3 copies (¶1.04–1.05, pp.130–131; Verified). O&M manuals (4 hard, 2 PDF sets) go in draft with shop drawings, final draft before the 75% pay application, and complete before payment above 90% (¶1.05.G, pp.131–132; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 78), main spec pp.136–141; Wiki note 01 45 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1643)
nodes.label: 01 45 00 · Quality Control
nodes.summary: Splits inspection and testing between the parties: the Contractor keeps records of all inspections and tests, pays for repeat tests after any failure (including Owner-responsibility tests), gives 48 hours' notice before work needing inspection, and uses only Owner-approved laboratories (¶1.05.A–E, ¶1.06.C, pp.137–139; Verified). Contractor-paid: pipe pressure testing and potable water pipe disinfection per the technical sections, equipment testing per the equipment sections (Division 46, p.141), clean water leakage testing, and clean water mechanical testing of pumps, diffusers, mixers and air lift assemblies (¶1.05.B.1, p.137; Verified). Owner-paid, Contractor-coordinated: building special inspections for concrete and structural steel (the p.141 summary adds air barrier testing per WA Energy Code Section 402), earthwork, concrete, asphalt (Rice density, compaction, extraction/gradation), coatings and field welding (¶1.05.B.2, pp.137–138, p.141; Verified); the WSDOT/AASHTO compaction and asphalt testing standards (¶1.03.B, p.136) are Unresolved: external reference, not staged. Before startup, eight new structures get a fill-to-rim clean water leakage test held 2 hours with no visible leakage — influent pump station, flow splitter, aeration basins, anoxic basins, clarifier, UV disinfection chamber, digester, 2W water system pump station (¶1.09, pp.139–140; Verified; repeated in 01 50 00 — Issues 1.22). The Owner's on-site representative cannot change the contract or accept work, and missed defects can still be rejected later (¶1.07–1.08, p.139; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 79), main spec pp.142–145; Wiki note 01 50 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1659)
nodes.label: 01 50 00 · Temporary Facilities
nodes.summary: The Contractor arranges all temporary utilities; a field office is encouraged but not required, while water and sanitation must be provided for all workers (¶1.01.A–B, p.142; Verified; field office conflicts with 01 31 00 — Issues 1.16). Required facilities: temporary power and lighting to the closest utility source, metered construction water with backflow prevention if agreed, temporary restrooms, drinking water, protected storage, first aid per WAC 296-24, and access at all times to homes, the WWTP and water treatment plant, and the helicopter pad for emergency vehicles (¶1.04.A–G, I, pp.142–144; Verified). Wastewater bypass systems are required for both influent and effluent; bypass pumping and other temporary process equipment need continuous oversight by on-site staff or an alarm with automatic cellular notification, 24/7 call-out with on-site response within 30 minutes, and backup alarms and running status wired to the District's existing control system, with PLC/SCADA programming incidental (¶1.01.D.2, ¶1.04.H, pp.142–144; Verified).
