The clean water leakage test repeats 01 45 00 but groups the aeration basins, anoxic basins and clarifier under Train #3 and names UV channels #1 and #2 and the 2W pump station wet well (¶1.04.C, p.143; Verified; Issues 1.22). Cleanup, noise, dust, erosion control per 31 32 11, pollution control and barriers at all hazards close the section (¶1.05–1.08, pp.144–145; Verified; barrier text repeats 00 73 00 SC 23), and temporary items come out at completion of the work (¶1.01.C, ¶1.04.A.4, ¶1.04.B.3, ¶1.04.D.1; removal timing conflicts with 01 70 00 — Issues 1.19).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 82), main spec pp.152–156; Wiki note 01 70 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1707)
nodes.label: 01 70 00 · Execution and Closeout Requirements
nodes.summary: Before requesting Substantial Completion the Contractor delivers tools, spare parts and extra stock, changes over locks and hands over keys, completes start-up testing and operator instruction, removes temporary facilities, turns over record information, finishes cleanup, and provides O&M manuals for all equipment, controls, telemetry and SCADA plus 2015 WSEC compliance documentation per C103.6.3 (¶1.03.A, pp.152–153; Verified; temporary facility removal conflicts with 00 73 00 SC 19 — Issues 1.19; energy code edition — Issues 1.20). The request carries a completion notice, incomplete-items list, pay request, change accounting, warranties and bonds, releases and occupancy/operating certificates, and record documents; "substantially complete" is defined by the WSDOT General Specifications and "Sections 00 72 00 and 00 73 00a" (¶1.03.B, p.153; WSDOT part Unresolved: external reference, not staged; section numbers — Issues 2.5), and warranties start on the Date of Substantial Completion (¶1.03.D.1, p.153; Verified; bears on Issues 1.11). Retainage is released only against an affidavit of paid payrolls and bills, lien releases, the DOR tax form, the L&I affidavit of wages paid and the ESD release (¶1.05.B, p.154; Verified). All mechanical and electrical equipment is tested before any facility goes into operation: procedures due 14 days before start-up covering every control device, equipment item and control circuit, joint sign-off forms, testing witnessed by the Engineer, and manufacturers' representatives who train Owner staff and certify each installation by letter (¶1.06, p.155; Verified). A daily record print set and a marked-up project manual are kept on site, then final cleanup (¶1.07–1.10, pp.155–156; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 83), main spec pp.157–160; Wiki note 01 91 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1723)
nodes.label: 01 91 00 · Commissioning
nodes.summary: Sets minimum supplier start-up supervision and operator training as a non-exhaustive checklist; every entry covers installation inspection, motor amperage checks, access, controls operation, an O&M manual review and controls training (¶1.01.B, pp.157–160; Verified). Minimums: influent pump station submersible pumps 5 days; Train 3 biological treatment equipment 2 weeks (clarifier drive, mixers, valves, DO and pH sensors, air lift pumps; weirs and baffles set level); blowers 2 days; UV system 2 days (intensity monitoring); peristaltic WAS and digested sludge pumps 2 days (¶1.02–1.06, pp.157–158; Verified). Dewatering equipment suppliers each give "a minimum of one (2) days" (¶1.07, p.159; Unresolved — Issues 1.21); the 2W water system supplier 1 day, verifying constant 60–90 psi from 0 to 50 gpm, the automatic valve at the air gap and the floats; the magnetic flow meter supplier 2 days, checking that submerged units are sealed and rated (¶1.10–1.11, pp.159–160; Verified). Paragraph numbers jump from 1.07 to 1.10 and ¶1.11 starts at "B" (p.159; Issues 2.8). No paragraph covers the generators, transfer switch, MCC or PLC panel — the list is stated as not exhaustive (¶1.01.B.3; Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 84), main spec pp.161–162; Wiki note 02 41 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1733)
nodes.label: 02 41 00 · Demolition
nodes.summary: Covers demolition, removal, rehabilitation and equipment salvage shown on the drawings; removed items become the Contractor's property except miscellaneous valves, piping and electronic components the Owner selects for salvage (¶1.01 B, ¶1.02 A; main spec p.161 — Verified). All pipes connected to abandoned structures are plugged or grouted, proposed wastewater equipment must be purchased and on hand before specified structures are removed, and removal is coordinated with the Owner's staff at least 2 weeks ahead (¶3.01 B; p.161 — Verified). Structures to be removed: the existing septic tank, the existing pump sump pump station, and miscellaneous valves, piping, concrete and accessories per the plans, with electrical drawings and specifications for more demolition (¶3.01 C; p.162 — Verified). Debris is hauled to a legal disposal site and no burning is allowed on site (¶3.02; p.162 — Verified). The section has no submittal or testing paragraph; the demolition plan with schedule is a C0.5 General Note requirement (p.161–162 — Verified; C0.5, plans_2Part-4 p.1 — Verified-Visual).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 85), main spec pp.163–168; Wiki note 02 83 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1741)
nodes.label: 02 83 00 · Chain Link Fences and Gates
nodes.summary: All chain-link fence and gates are 6-ft galvanized fabric with 3-strand barbed wire on top (7 ft total), with bottom rails to stop access under the fabric (¶1.01 A; main spec p.163 — Verified). Submittals: three samples (fabric, post section, accessories) and shop drawings showing height, fabric, post and gate locations and sizes, footings and hardware (¶1.04; p.163 — Verified). Materials: ASTM A392 No. 9 gage 2-in mesh Class II galvanized fabric, Sch. 40 posts (2.375-in line, 2.875-in end/corner/pull, 4-in or 6-5/8-in gate posts by leaf width), 1.66-in rails and braces, swing or non-motorized rolling gates with locking latches (¶2.01–2.09; pp.164–166 — Verified). Line posts at 10 ft maximum, concrete-set, with fabric hung no sooner than 5 days after posts are set; fence under or within 50 ft of a primary power line is grounded (¶3.04, ¶3.06, ¶3.08; pp.167–168 — Verified). Cross-references use older numbers: 'Section 05500' and 'Section 03300' (¶1.02 A, ¶2.10 A; pp.163, 166 — Verified; see Issues).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 86), main spec pp.169–171; Wiki note 02 92 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1749)
nodes.label: 02 92 00 · Landscaping
nodes.summary: Covers re-establishing grass in areas disturbed by construction: stripping, stockpiling, topsoil, compost and hydroseeding, with a one-year seeding guarantee and 2 in of straw on graded areas not seeded or paved by October 15 (¶1.1, ¶1.3; main spec p.169 — Verified). Submittals: product data and installation recommendations, seed vendor blue-tag certification, and maintenance instructions after acceptance (¶1.03; p.169 — Verified). Seed is Sunmark 'DOT Multipurpose Mixture' at 8 lb/1,000 SF, fertilizer 6.5 lb/1,000 SF, wood fiber mulch 2,000 lb/acre, seeding August 15 to October 15 (¶2.2–2.4, ¶3.1 F–H; pp.170–171 — Verified). Topsoil follows 'Section 9.14.1(2) of the Standard Specifications' and hydroseeding follows WSDOT 8-01.3(2)B (¶2.1, ¶3.1 E; pp.170–171 — Verified; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). ¶2.2 B names 'R.I. Galleries' and a 'field behind recreation center', which appear on no Civil & Site sheet (p.170 — Verified; see Issues).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 87), main spec pp.172–180; Wiki note 03 30 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1761)
nodes.label: 03 30 00 · Cast-in-Place Concrete
nodes.summary: Covers labor, materials and equipment for subgrade preparation, forms, rebar and placement of all cast-in-place concrete shown, paid as incidental to the lump-sum bid items in which the work appears; the only extra-work items are overexcavation and structural fill under 31 20 00, by written authorization [¶1.01 A.1, ¶1.03, p.172 — Verified]. The Drawing Structural Notes take precedence over less specific spec requirements and set the mix designs and reinforcing, while WSDOT M41-10 (2022), WSDOT material sources, WSDOT-approved aggregate sources and WSDOT 9-04.2 joint sealant are incorporated by reference [¶1.05 A, ¶2.03 A, ¶2.04 B–C, pp.172–175 — Verified; ¶1.04 A.1, ¶1.06 D.4, ¶2.04 A, ¶2.04 D — Unresolved: external reference, not staged]. Submittals are ACI SP-66 shop drawings, mix designs 15 working days before use, material certificates, a PE-prepared hot and cold weather plan, joint layout plans (control joints no more than 30× slab thickness where not shown), and WA SE-sealed formwork plans and calculations for the "Clarifier, digester and chlorine contact basin structures" — names that do not all match the sheet titles [¶1.06 A–G, p.173 — Verified; Issues, Missing information]. The Owner provides independent testing and inspection (subgrade compaction and moisture, reinforcing placement, concrete placement and cylinders) and special inspections, and anchor bolts are set to AISC 303-16 §7.5 tolerances by a registered land surveyor [¶1.07 B, p.174; ¶3.012 A, p.180; ¶3.03 B, p.176 — Verified]. Products and execution include hydrophilic waterstop (Cetco RX-101T or Greenstreak Hydrotite CJ0725, 3" min. cover), 15-mil Stego Wrap vapor retarder, 40-diameter laps unless shown otherwise, steel-trowel interior slabs damp-cured only with 1/8"/ft grout slopes to sumps, and a moist cure of 90 days min. for all structural concrete against 7 days for building slabs [¶2.04 F, ¶2.05, ¶3.05 B, ¶3.09 A.1, ¶3.010 D, pp.175–179 — Verified; cure duration — Unresolved, Issues, Conflicts].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 88), main spec pp.181–185; Wiki note 03 40 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1775)
nodes.label: 03 40 00 · Precast Concrete
nodes.summary: Covers design, supply and installation of all precast concrete structures shown — vaults, top slabs and "the effluent wet well" — with WA-engineer-sealed shop drawings and calculations, mix designs 15 days ahead, material certificates, 5 years of NPCA certification, and Owner/Engineer plant inspection rights [¶1.01 A, p.181; ¶1.06 A–F, ¶1.07, p.182 — Verified; WSDOT M41-10 references ¶1.04 C and ¶1.05 B — Unresolved: external reference, not staged]. Wet wells and vaults are 5,000 psi with A615 Gr 60 rebar to ACI 318-14 and ASTM C857: 96" Oldcastle wet wells with 48"×30" H-20 aluminum hatches (LW Products HD-3C) at the 2W Plant Water Pump Station (C4.2) and Influent Pump Station (C4.1), and 4'×4' Oldcastle 4686-LA vaults with 36"×36" H-20 single-leaf hatches (Halliday H1R3636) for the Influent and Effluent Flow Meter Valve Vaults and Plants 2 & 3 Flow Meter Vault (C7.4) and the Influent Pump Station Meter Vaults (C4.1) [¶2.02 E, p.183 — Verified]. The top slab schedule separately calls for the Influent Pump Station top slab per the Contract Plan details with a new 3'-0"×5'-0" light-duty aluminum hatch with safety grates (Flygt FLED-13 or equal), which conflicts with the 48"×30" H-20 hatch in the vault table [¶2.02 D.1 and E.2, p.183 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues, Conflicts]. Accessories are non-shrink grout (6,000 psi at 7 days) for anchor bolt and handrail pockets and non-mechanical base plates, 1:2 Portland cement grout (4,000 psi) for wall-slab slopes, ASTM C881 Type IV epoxy grout for pump bases, RAM-NEK or Quikseal sealant gaskets, and Canusa WrapidSeal heat-shrink external joint sleeves [¶2.02 F–I, p.184 — Verified], which Add. 4 applies to the exterior of all precast wet well and vault joints [Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 2 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Installation requires watertight gasketed joints, primed heat-shrink sleeves with 3 days' notice by a manufacturer-trained installer, backfill compacted to 95% within 4 ft of vault walls, frames set within 1/4" vertical, and hatches machined for a solid fit [¶3.02 B–G, p.185 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 89), main spec pp.186–199; Wiki note 05 50 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1789)
nodes.label: 05 50 00 · Metal Fabrications
nodes.summary: Covers metal fabrications that are not structural steel or other specified metal systems — embedded and non-embedded metal work, anchor bolts, beams, bracing, framing and supports for mechanical and electrical equipment, shelf angles, metal ladders and ship ladders, and metal pipe and tube railings — related to 03 30 00, 13 12 20 and 09 90 00 [¶1.01 A–B, ¶1.02, p.186 — Verified]. Submittals are shop drawings for all fabricated items, product data, nosing samples, PE qualification data, stainless mill certificates, paint compatibility certificates and welder certificates, with welding to AWS D1.1/D1.6 by state-licensed welders [¶1.04, p.187; ¶1.05 B, p.187; ¶2.04 A, p.192 — Verified]. Ferrous metal not fully embedded in concrete is hot-dip galvanized after fabrication (2 oz/sf min.), aluminum touching concrete gets bituminous paint, and all-thread hanger rod is allowed only in stainless [¶2.02 D, p.191; ¶2.010, p.193; ¶3.04 A, p.197; ¶2.08, p.193 — Verified]. Mechanical anchors are limited to non-water-bearing concrete (building slabs, walkways, Engineer-approved locations), and chemical anchors are required on all water-bearing structures and wherever spacing or edge distance is under 3.5" [¶2.03 B, pp.191–192 — Verified]. Handrails and guardrails are specified here as 1-1/4" steel pipe (ASTM A53 Gr B) while ¶2.02 B specifies aluminum pipe railings, and grouting is referred to a Section 04 60 00 that exists neither in the main spec nor in 02 [¶2.014 A, p.196; ¶2.02 B.1, p.191; ¶3.03 E, p.197 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 90), main spec pp.200–202; Wiki note 05 51 10 (Project_Wiki.md line 1803)
nodes.label: 05 51 10 · Steel Stairs, Ladders and Grating Platforms
nodes.norm_label: 05 51 10 · steel stairs, ladders and grating platforms
nodes.summary: The Contractor designs, details, fabricates and installs galvanized steel stairs, ladders and platform framing where shown on the plans, with non-skid grating treads and aluminum grating platforms [¶1.01 A.1, p.200 — Verified]. Submittals are PE-sealed calculations and location-specific shop drawings (typical-detail sets are rejected), coordinated with the grating drawings and with aluminum handrails "as shown in the civil drawings" per 05 52 00 and 05 53 00 [¶1.03 A.1–3, p.200 — Verified], matching the deferred submittal for metal stairs and landings on S1.1 [plans_7 p.8 — Verified-Visual]. The Drawing Structural Notes govern over less specific requirements, with AISC 360, AWS D1.1 (2015) and IBC 2018 as standards, and all framing is hot-dip galvanized after fabrication and bolted in the field [¶1.04 A–D, p.200; ¶2.03, p.201 — Verified]. Unless shown otherwise, stairs use 7" risers, 11" treads and 1" nosing with 4'-0" min. clear width, access ladders have 3'-0" min. clear width, and field welding needs written approval at shop drawing review [¶2.04, p.201; ¶3.01 D, p.202 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 91), main spec pp.203–204; Wiki note 05 52 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1817)
nodes.label: 05 52 00 · Aluminum Handrailing and Guardrailing
nodes.summary: Aluminum handrails (two horizontal bars) and guardrails (6" sphere rule) are provided where shown, with height, picket spacing and toe plates detailed on the Civil Drawings, to OSHA and IBC 2018 [¶1.01 A–B, p.203 — Verified]. Submittals are shop drawings with a dimensional layout, the manufacturer's assembly and installation instructions, and calculations sealed by a Washington State registered structural engineer; partial or unsealed submittals are rejected [¶1.02 A–B, p.203 — Verified]. Rails, posts and stanchions are 1-1/2" IPS Schedule 40 aluminum with a clear satin anodized Class I finish (0.7 mil min.) from Golden Railing, CRL or Ametco or equal, with 3/16" min. aluminum toeboards on all guardrails [Part 2 A–B, p.203 — Verified]. Connections to structure use Type 316 stainless bolts, posts and rails get weep holes, removable sections mount independently, aluminum touching concrete gets bituminous paint, and embedded posts are grouted into blockouts after the concrete reaches design strength [¶3.01 B–D, ¶3.02 A–B, p.204 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 92), main spec pp.205–206; Wiki note 05 53 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1831)
nodes.label: 05 53 00 · Grating
nodes.summary: Scope is aluminum grating set in pultruded vinyl ester FRP embedment angles with an integral anchor, to the NAAMM Metal Bar Grating Manual, with shop drawings and manufacturer's instructions as the submittal (the paragraph asks for a "dimensional layout of all handrailing," as written) [¶1.01 A, ¶1.02 A, ¶1.03 A, p.205 — Verified]. Solid plank grating is for UV channels only: 2" all-aluminum slip-resistant plank (SlipNOT or equal) that blocks all light from leaving the UV channel, on embedment angles per the grating manufacturer [¶2.01 A–C, p.205 — Verified]. Aluminum bar grating carries 100 psf at L/360 (2.0" deep, 4.0 lb/sf for 2'-6" to 6'-7" spans), is banded I-bar, and sits flush on 2"×2"×1/4" gray pultruded FRP embedment angles (IKG or equal) [¶2.02 A–C, p.205 — Verified]. Grating is fastened with removable aluminum clips and Type 316 stainless bolts, with galvanic isolation and bituminous paint where aluminum meets concrete or grout [¶3.01 A–C, p.206 — Verified]; S2.2 instead supports the grating on HDG steel angles and calls solid plank grating as typical at both basins [plans_8 p.2, Details 5–6 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved — Issues, Conflicts].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 94), main spec pp.209–210; Wiki note 07 20 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1859)
nodes.label: 07 20 00 · Insulation
nodes.summary: Covers thermal insulation and vapor barrier in exterior roof and wall construction, installed by a metal building insulation installer with 3 years' experience; materials arrive with instructions and typical shop drawings, and the section has no separate submittal article [¶1.1 A, ¶1.2 A–B, p.209 — Verified]. The system is the Thermal Design Simple Saver interior finish and insulation system or equal — steel straps, woven reinforced polyethylene liner fabric with welded seams, sealants and tapes — with exposed parts at flame spread 25 or less and smoke developed 50 or less (ASTM E84) [¶1.2 C, ¶2.1 A–B, p.209 — Verified]. Insulation is unfaced fiberglass batt to the in-place R-value noted on the drawings (ASTM C518) with 1/8" × 3" XPS thermal blocks, and the vapor barrier goes on the interior side, continuous and taped at all joints and penetrations [¶2.2 A–B, p.209; ¶3.1 A–C, p.210 — Verified]; A1.1 sets R-25 walls and R-30 roof on furring with GWB walls, an assembly that differs from the liner system [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved — Issues, Conflicts]. The section does not cover the R-10 XPS footing-perimeter insulation or the Dryvit EIFS shown on A1.2, and 02 lists no other Division 07 section except 07 92 00 [¶1.1 A, p.209; plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; 02 index — Verified; Unresolved — Issues, Missing information].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 96), main spec pp.214–215; Wiki note 08 10 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1887)
nodes.label: 08 10 00 · Metal Doors and Frames
nodes.summary: Exterior insulated hollow metal (INS HM) doors are standard-duty, full flush, SDI 100 Grade II Model 1 with polyurethane or polyisocyanurate core and 18-gauge minimum faces, of cold-rolled A366 steel hot-dip galvanized to A526 G90 with factory baked-on primer [¶2.01 A, ¶2.02 A, pp.214–215 — Verified]. Frames are one-piece welded, 16-gauge minimum, galvanized, with integral stops, SDI 100 Grade II Model 2, and tempered glass windows are provided only where the door schedule calls for them [¶2.02 B–C, p.215 — Verified]. Hardware is furnished under 08 70 00 and installed here per SDI 107, doors install per SDI 105 with hardware adjusted and lubricated, and the section has no submittal or testing article of its own [¶1.01 A, ¶2.01 B, ¶3.01, pp.214–215 — Verified]. The matching items are A1.1's insulated hollow metal doors 101A, 101B and 101C (Types A and B, no glass) [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 97), main spec pp.216–224; Wiki note 08 70 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1901)
nodes.label: 08 70 00 · Finish Hardware
nodes.summary: Covers all finish hardware (quantities not guaranteed), with submittals of manufacturer's data, a hardware schedule in sets cross-referenced to the door schedule, a keying schedule and templates; closers carry a 5-year and other hardware a 1-year guarantee [¶1.01 A, ¶1.03 A–E, ¶1.05 A, pp.216–218 — Verified]. Part 4 sets Hardware Group 1 (exterior single INS HM doors) and Group 2 (exterior double doors): Stanley FBB179 hinges, Corbin Russwin ML2000 mortise locksets with Lustra lever trim keyed to the District standard, Ives 458 flush bolts and DP2 strike, Sargent 421 closers, kickplates, Pemko 357SP astragal, S88D gasketing and 315SN sweeps, National Guard 713 thresholds and Ives FS446 exterior stops [Part 4, pp.223–224 — Verified]; A1.1 assigns no group, so doors map by type [Inferred]. ¶2.03 A instead calls key-in-knob cylindrical locksets keyed to the "Upper Skagit Indian Tribe standard," and ¶2.07 A points the exterior door stop detail to sheet C8.1, which 01 does not list [¶2.03 A, p.219; ¶2.07 A, p.220 — Verified; 01 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues]. ¶2.08 A adds one concrete pad with a Gempler's #2900 boot and shoe brush with scraper next to the Blower Building exterior door, location coordinated with the Owner [p.220 — Verified]. Execution requires adjusting and checking every operating item, instructing the Owner's staff, a return visit about six months after acceptance to re-adjust all hardware with a written report, and 2 sets of special tools [¶3.04 A–E, ¶3.05, p.222 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 98), main spec pp.225–228; Wiki note 09 25 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1915)
nodes.label: 09 25 00 · Gypsum Drywall
nodes.summary: Covers all gypsum drywall shown, taped and spackled, to ASTM C840 from a single source, with texture finish samples as the only submittal [¶1.01 A, ¶1.02 A–B, ¶1.03 A, p.225 — Verified]. Board is 5/8" USG Aqua-Tough (green board) unless noted, Type X at fire-rated assemblies and Fiberock at high-moisture locations, with ASTM C1002 screws, Dur-A-Bead corners, LC and L beads, Perf-A-Tape and USG Imperial QT spray texture [¶2.01 A–E, p.226 — Verified]. Board fastens to steel framing with self-drilling screws at 12" o.c. max., gets a 3-coat joint finish sanded between coats, and hollow metal door frames are spot-grouted at the jamb anchors [¶3.02 H, ¶3.02 L.1, ¶3.03 D, pp.227–228 — Verified]. Texture primer is referred to "Section 09900 Painting"; Add. 4 adds 09 90 00 Service Condition J for the Blower Building's gypsum board, which matches the painted GWB walls in the A1.1 finish schedule [¶3.04 A, p.228 — Verified; Add. 4 p.2 — Verified; plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 99), main spec pp.229–235; Wiki note 09 90 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1929)
nodes.label: 09 90 00 · Misc. Plant Painting
nodes.status: Main spec pp.229–235 · Addendum 4: Add. 4 p.2, ¶2.01 I — Add. 4 governs
nodes.summary: Covers preparation and application of paint coatings, but ¶1.01 A sends the new Blower Building and masonry, concrete and stucco painting to a "09 90 00 – Paints and Coatings" section that exists in neither the main spec nor 02 [¶1.01 A, p.229 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues, Missing information]. Submittals are product data and procedures per service condition, color charts 30 days and a painting schedule 14 days before work; the Contractor measures wet-film thickness of every coat, the Engineer approves each coat, and hold points follow surface preparation and final coating [¶1.03 A–C, ¶1.02 E, p.229; ¶3.03 D, p.234; ¶3.06, p.235 — Verified]. Service conditions are A epoxy (Tnemec 161 or SW Macropoxy 646) on exposed metal piping, valves, supports and misc. ferrous metal but not galvanized, aluminum or stainless; B interior wood; C metal doors and frames (two coats SW Industrial Enamel, DF 4.0, over factory primer); D PVC piping; E exterior wood stain; and H non-skid epoxy at the headworks floor [¶2.01 I.1–6, pp.231–232 — Verified]. Add. 4 adds Service Condition J for the new Blower Building gypsum board: one coat Sherwin-Williams wall primer (DF 2.0) and two coats Sherwin-Williams Pro-Mar alkyd egg-shell (DF 4.0) [Add. 4 p.2, 09 90 00 ¶2.01 I — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Execution requires concrete cured 28 days before painting, galvanized surfaces passivated before priming, and exposed piping painted and labeled by service (for example, 2W light blue, air white) with a labeling walk-through before Substantial Completion [¶3.02 G and L, pp.233–234; ¶3.05, p.235 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 100), main spec pp.236–241; Wiki note 09 97 23 (Project_Wiki.md line 1943)
nodes.label: 09 97 23 · Concrete Protective Coating
nodes.summary: Covers a spray-applied, monolithic, high-build 100%-solids epoxy lining on all interior concrete surfaces of the listed structure — the Influent Pump Station, with detailed locations per the drawings [¶1.01 A–B, p.236 — Verified]. Submittals are product data with ASTM results, MSDS, project guidelines and applicator qualifications (manufacturer certification, trained equipment operators, 5 references, permits) [¶1.02 A, p.236 — Verified]. The product is Raven 405 or Tnemec G436 PermaShield (amine-cured, light green), applied by a certified applicator with heated plural-component spray on concrete cured at least 28 days and blasted to CSP 3–5, at 80 mils min. and 100 mils average wet film [¶2.01 A, ¶2.04 A, ¶2.05, ¶3.03 E, ¶3.05 D, pp.237–239 — Verified]. Testing covers wet-film readings (ASTM D4414), optional ultrasonic dry-film checks (SSPC-PA 9), high-voltage holiday testing at 100 V/mil (NACE RP0188 or ASTM D4787), and pull-off adhesion (ASTM D7234) with 2 of 3 pulls over 200 psi per test area, all documented to the Owner [¶3.06 A–D, pp.239–241 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 101), main spec pp.242–242; Wiki note 10 52 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 1957)
nodes.label: 10 52 00 · Fire Extinguishers
nodes.summary: Covers furnishing and installing all fire extinguishers and cabinets shown, with product data (plus cabinet roughing-in and mounting details) as the submittal [¶1.01 A–B, ¶1.02 A, p.242 — Verified]. Extinguishers are J.L. Industries Cosmic 5E, UL 2A-10BC, standard red, on the manufacturer's standard brackets that prevent accidental dislodgment [¶2.01 A–B, p.242 — Verified]. At completion the work is visually inspected and checked for proper operation, and each extinguisher carries an inspection tag [¶3.01 C, p.242 — Verified]. The Blower Building gets 2 wall-mounted assemblies per Add. 4, where base A1.1 shows 1 [Add. 4 p.4 — Verified; plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 governs].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 102), main spec pp.243–245; Wiki note 10 73 05 (Project_Wiki.md line 1968)
nodes.label: 10 73 05 · FRP Launder Covers
nodes.summary: The contractor furnishes and installs a molded, UV-protected, opaque FRP cover over the Train 3 clarifier weir launder and weir, in curved sections at least 4 ft long, each a single section on two pivoting brackets opening toward the tank center, with spring-loaded latches, an optional stainless tether, fixed or vertical panels at the bridge support, no piano hinges, no inspection hatches, and not walk-on except for a reinforced walk-on section at the launder entry (¶1.01 A–H pp.243–244). Panels are isophthalic polyester with UV suppression, at least 35% glass by weight (ASTM D2584-18), nominal 1/4" thick and no more than 55 lb each, with tensile 26,000 psi, flexural 30,000 psi, flexural modulus 1.9×10^6 psi, Barcol 50, notched Izod 20 ft-lb/in and water absorption 0.25% max; fasteners, handles, hinges and latches are stainless (¶3.01 B–G pp.244–245). Submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data and O&M information (¶2.01 A p.244); the contractor adds a 1-year parts-and-labor extended warranty from substantial completion (¶1.02 A p.244); three sets of wear parts are furnished (¶3.02 p.245); and the manufacturer provides installation certification, 2 days of start-up and field testing and 1 day of operator training (¶4.02 p.245). ¶3.01 A, under the launder cover heading, repeats the packaged sludge pump paragraph of 22 13 36 ¶2.01 A word for word (Edson peristaltic pumps, 3 HP, a VFD per pump) — Issue 20. The section runs in four parts (Part 2 submittals, Part 3 products, Part 4 execution).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 103), main spec pp.246–251; Wiki note 13 12 20 (Project_Wiki.md line 1981)
nodes.label: 13 12 20 · Metal Building Systems
nodes.status: Main spec pp.246–251 · Addendum 4: Cited, no change — Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 3 (¶2.03, ¶2.04)
nodes.summary: Covers a rigid-frame, bolted, pre-manufactured metal building with galvanized cold-formed secondary members and pre-coated metal roofing and siding, for the Blower Building and the existing building modifications shown on A1.3 [¶1.01 A–B, p.246 — Verified]. Design loads — 5 psf collateral, 25 psf snow, 20 psf roof live, 105 mph ultimate wind (Exposure C), Site Class D with SDS 0.79 / SD1 0.51, SDC D, Ie 1.25, 18" frost — match S1.1, and submittals are WA SE-sealed design calculations and drawings for permit, a WA SE-sealed anchor bolt embedment design by the Contractor, and erection drawings [¶1.03 A, p.246; ¶1.04 A–B, p.247 — Verified; plans_7 p.8 — Verified-Visual]. Garco Building Systems or equal (AISC Category MB certified, MBMA member) supplies 50 ksi hot-dip galvanized primary framing, G-90 16-gauge secondary members, A325 bolts, galvanized cable or rod bracing, 24-gauge Galvalume standing-seam roof panels (UL 90) and 26-gauge Galvalume R- or A-type wall panels, factory-finished in polyester or Kynar at the Owner's choice [¶1.05, ¶2.01–¶2.04, pp.247–249 — Verified; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 3 — Verified]. ¶2.05 A.1 describes the Blower Building as a rigid frame of "42' bldg. width, 9.75' bldg. length" with 9'-0" minimum haunch clearance, which Add. 4 supersedes with a 44.00' × 9.25' footprint and 10.25' clearance [p.249 — Verified; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 4, p.4, p.5 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Installers need 5 years' experience, anchor bolts and base plates are verified against the approved erection drawings, bolts are tightened by turn-of-nut (preferred), and panels are lapped and butyl-sealed with trim and closures for a weather-tight enclosure; the section has no testing article [¶3.01–¶3.03, pp.250–251 — Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 104), main spec pp.252–252; Wiki note 15 08 13 (Project_Wiki.md line 1991)
nodes.label: 15 08 13 · Temporary Construction Sign
nodes.summary: The Contractor supplies and erects a temporary construction sign to Department of Ecology and CDBG Department of Commerce requirements (Part 1 ¶A; main spec p.252 — Verified). The sign is 4 ft x 8 ft x 3/4-in APA A-B exterior plywood, black lettering on white, with Ecology, CDBG Commerce, Engineer and Contractor logos (¶1.02 A.1–4; p.252 — Verified). Text includes the project name with loan number WQC-2021-EaSoWd-00208, the Owner, San Juan County, Wilson Engineering and the Contractor (¶1.02 A.5; p.252 — Verified). Submittal: proof of graphics before printing (¶1.01; p.252 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 105), main spec pp.253–254; Wiki note 15 40 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2000)
nodes.label: 15 40 00 · Misc. Plumbing
nodes.summary: Covers miscellaneous plumbing "for exterior purposes only" as described and shown on the plans (¶1.01 A p.253), with shop drawing and product data submittals (¶1.02 A) and compliance with the UBC, UPC and Eastsound Sewer and Water District standards (¶1.03 A). Materials: ABS DWV soil and waste piping above and below ground, unions at equipment connections, full-size cleanouts ("provide brass lugs, with graphite lubricant on threads"), 1" frost-proof yard hydrants (stainless rod and pipe, automatic draining, backflow preventer, 3/4" hose thread, Smith Cooper 0190167II vacuum breaker or equal, 4' bury; Woodford Iowa Y2 or Merrill CV-1000 or equal), and 2" post hydrants (316 SS hardware, 304 SS lower stem rod, hand wheel, brass working parts, 4' bury; American AVK Dry Barrel 67XX or Eclipse No. 2A or equal) with 2" Danfoss AVB atmospheric vacuum breakers (125 psi, ASSE 1001) (¶2.01 A–E p.253). Installation slopes drains 1/4" per foot, provides code cleanouts and follows manufacturer instructions and local codes (¶3.01 p.254); no testing is specified. No sheet in the P&M stack shows hydrant or drain locations or quantities (cross-lane item for Merge).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 106), main spec pp.255–262; Wiki note 22 13 29 (Project_Wiki.md line 2010)
nodes.label: 22 13 29 · Submersible Sewerage Pumps
nodes.status: Main spec pp.255–262 · Header spelling — see conflict log
nodes.summary: A performance specification for the complete, tested Influent Pump Station — pumps, controls, discharge piping, vaults, flow meter and connection to existing piping — with the contractor responsible for field measurements and supplier coordination (¶1.01 A–E p.255). Pump schedule (¶2.02 B p.258): two small pumps, Flygt N3085 MT, 150 gpm @ 20.5 ft design (120 gpm @ 22.0 ft; 220 gpm @ 17.5 ft; shutoff 26 ft), 2.7 HP, 1800 rpm, 43% minimum efficiency, 135 mm Adaptive N-impeller, 3 1/8" discharge; two large pumps, Flygt N3102 MT, 385 gpm @ 20.5 ft (320 gpm @ 22.5 ft; 500 gpm @ 15.0 ft; shutoff 38 ft), 5.0 HP, 1800 rpm, 66%, 152 mm impeller, 3 15/16" discharge; all 460 V 3-phase, rated Class 1 Division 1 Groups C and D, one manufacturer for all (¶2.01 C; ¶2.02 C.1, C.9 pp.257–260). Each pump has a cast-iron discharge connection with a machined metal-to-metal seal, two 316 SS guide bars about 15 ft long (contractor to verify), 316 SS brackets and a 20 ft stainless lifting chain with spectra cord for a Grip-Eye device, three 316 SS cable holders, a Flygt MiniCAS-120 motor saver relay supplied to the Control Systems Integrator, and pressure gages (Marsh P0142, 0–25 psi) with Branom diaphragm isolators and Apollo shutoff valves (¶2.02 C.2, C.10, F; ¶2.03; ¶2.04 pp.259–261). Submittals include certified curves, shop drawings of the station and lifting system, control panel and interconnection wiring, warranty and factory test report (¶1.03 A p.256); testing includes certified non-witnessed factory performance tests to Hydraulic Institute standards, a factory operational test of the completed station submitted before installation, field tests with the manufacturer's representative, and at least one 8-hour start-up day with flow tests (¶1.03 C, ¶1.04 B–C p.256; ¶3.03 p.262). The warranty is 5 years or 10,000 hours (¶1.05 A p.256), and float switches hang at the plan levels with a submersible level transducer also used for pump control (¶3.02 A p.261).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 107), main spec pp.263–264; Wiki note 22 13 36 (Project_Wiki.md line 2020)
nodes.label: 22 13 36 · Packaged Sludge Pumps
nodes.status: Main spec pp.263–264 · Addendum 4: Add. 4 p.2, ¶2.01 A — Add. 4 governs
nodes.summary: Furnish and install three sludge pumps — one WAS pump, one digested sludge pump and one swing pump for either service — for dilute sludge at 0.5% to 3.0% solids (¶1.01 A–B p.263). Base ¶2.01 A (p.263) calls for Edson Platinum peristaltic pumps or equal, 3 HP, 460 V, 3-phase, 0 to 43 gpm (typical set point 10 to 30 gpm), corrosion resistant, with a VFD and a local speed dial per pump, an electrical control panel per pump and a 304 SS enclosure of about 40"×40"×40" per pump. Add. 4 p.2 replaces "Each pump is to include a VFD" with: pumps powered from VFDs in the Motor Control Center, VFDs controlled by the PLC in the Main Control Panel, no local speed control dial at the pump, see Electrical Sheets — Add. 4 governs. Controls follow 26 80 00 ¶3.09 A (WAS pump control) and H (rotary fan press system) (¶2.02 p.263); submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data with wiring diagrams and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.263); the manufacturer furnishes three sets of wear parts (¶2.03 p.263) and provides installation certification, 2 days of start-up and field testing and 1 day of operator training (¶3.02 p.264).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 108), main spec pp.265–267; Wiki note 23 34 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2030)
nodes.discipline: Process-Mechanical (lane per 02, decision D; cross-check E9.3 and A sheets)
nodes.label: 23 34 00 · Wall Fans and Louvered Vents
nodes.summary: Scope (¶1.01 A p.265): in the Blower Building, two 3,300 CFM wall fans on individual thermostats, one motorized 36"×84" louvered vent that opens when either fan runs and stays open until both are off, and one manual 24"×24" louvered vent; in the "Existing Dewatering/Train 1&2 Building Area", three 3,300 CFM wall fans on individual manual on/off switches and two manual 36"×84" louvered vents. Fans are Acme FQ18G6 (3,300 CFM, 1/2 HP, 120 V 1-phase, 12 sones max) with wall collar and guard, each with a Louvers & Dampers EBE445 aluminum gravity combination louver (about 24"×24") with stainless bird screen and a 2-year minimum manufacturer warranty; thermostats are Schaffer TH109 two-speed, 40–100°F, in NEMA 4X enclosures with stainless coil sensors, 4' above floor (¶1.01 B; ¶2.1 A–B pp.265–266). Vents are "Pottoroff" (as printed) EXD-645 combination louver/dampers with drainable blades, vinyl seals, washable 18×16 stainless insect screens and non-protruding actuation; the motorized unit uses a Pottoroff AF120 120 V spring-return actuator driven from the fan thermostat auxiliary contacts (¶2.2–2.3 pp.266–267). ¶2.1 A.4 calls all wall fans dual speed and thermostat controlled, while ¶1.01 A puts the three existing-building fans on manual switches (Issue 25). The section has no submittal or testing paragraph; installation follows the manufacturer's instructions, with controls 4' above floor (¶3.1 p.267).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 110), main spec pp.269–281; Wiki note 26 05 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2041)
nodes.label: 26 05 00 · General Electrical
nodes.summary: Drawings and specifications are complementary; motor horsepower on the drawings is an estimate for equipment furnished under other sections, with overloads sized to actual nameplate current (¶1.011 B–C, p.274) [Verified]. Submittals (¶1.012, p.274): electronic PDF with an index, identified by section and paragraph or equipment, each sheet naming the equipment and part number with manufacturer, model, nameplate data, dimensions and local representative; largely incomplete packages are returned unreviewed; variances requested in writing [Verified]. Construction power and downtime (¶1.015–1.016, p.276): the contractor provides and pays for a dedicated construction power service and its energy; power to the operating plant is kept at all times, with one week notice to the District before any utility disruption, and temporary equipment (generator, pumps, piping) plus an Owner/Engineer-approved written plan for any disruption over 20 minutes [Verified]. Utility interface (¶3.03, pp.279–280): OPALCO serves the site and the Owner pays utility charges; the contractor provides the new 480Y/277V underground secondary from the existing transformer pad to the CT enclosure, service-rated ATS and 400 A panel, the CT enclosure and meter bases, demolition of the existing 208V service (raceway, conductors, CT enclosure, meter base, generator, ATS) and temporary power to hold downtime to 20 minutes; the Utility removes the existing 208V transformer, sets the new 480V transformer on the existing pad and provides the CTs and meter [Verified]. Pads, tests and training (¶2.04, ¶3.04, ¶3.05, pp.278–280): a concrete housekeeping pad under each floor-mounted MCC and electrical equipment, 3 in wider each end and 3 in minimum height; feeder, motor and equipment testing and a functional checkout of every control circuit, with procedures submitted first; training of 8 h for electrical and 24 h for control systems [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 111), main spec pp.282–288; Wiki note 26 05 19 (Project_Wiki.md line 2051)
nodes.label: 26 05 19 · Wire and Cable
nodes.summary: Scope: 600 V conductors and cables for power, lighting, receptacle, signal and control; scheduled circuits per the drawings and schedules; lighting and receptacle circuits sized by the contractor to hold voltage drop to 3% (¶1.01, ¶2.01, p.282) [Verified]. Products: copper, stranded (12 AWG solid allowed for lighting and receptacles), 12 AWG minimum branch size; THHN/THWN for branch and control circuits and small power conductors, XHHW-2 for power conductors 6 AWG and larger; Okonite, Southwire or equal; compression connectors 8 AWG and larger; cast epoxy splices underground or in damp or corrosive locations (¶2.02–2.05, pp.282–283) [Verified]. Execution: shielded power cable from VFDs to motors where indicated; signal circuits in individually shielded twisted pairs or triads without splices, shields bonded at the control panel only; color code 480Y/277V brown-orange-yellow with gray neutral, 208Y/120V black-red-blue with white neutral, green ground, externally powered control wiring yellow (¶3.02 H, ¶3.03, ¶3.04, pp.285–286) [Verified]. Tests (¶3.07, pp.286–288): insulation resistance at 1,000 VDC for 30 s with 1 megohm minimum at 20 °C on scheduled power feeders and on service and feeder conductors; continuity; thermal imaging of all power terminations; ground resistance at each new rod, 25 ohms maximum per rod by the three-rod method and 15 ohms maximum composite; reports to the Engineer before final acceptance [Verified]. No product submittal paragraph in the section, read in full (pp.282–288) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 112), main spec pp.289–289; Wiki note 26 05 26 (Project_Wiki.md line 2061)
nodes.label: 26 05 26 · Grounding and Bonding
nodes.summary: Grounding per the NEC with soft-drawn bare stranded copper sized per the drawings; Burndy Hyground compression terminals and connectors; Cadweld or T&B exothermic welds; copper-clad rods with 0.010 in minimum cladding, 3/4 in x 8 ft minimum (¶1.01, ¶2.01, p.289) [Verified]. Installation: contact surfaces cleaned to bright metal; grounding conductors in PVC where subject to damage and all conductors smaller than 6 AWG protected; compression connections and splices; an equipment grounding conductor in every PVC conduit (¶3.01–3.02, p.289) [Verified]. No submittal or test paragraph; ground resistance testing sits in 26 05 19 ¶3.07 (25 ohms per rod, 15 ohms composite) (p.289; p.288) [Verified]. The rod size matches the E10.1 ground rod and handhole details (8 ft copper-clad) (p.289; plans_12 p.6) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 113), main spec pp.290–296; Wiki note 26 05 33 (Project_Wiki.md line 2071)
nodes.label: 26 05 33 · Raceways and Boxes
nodes.summary: Raceways for power, control, instrumentation, grounding, lighting, receptacles and signaling; scheduled raceway per the drawings, which prevail over ¶3.1 on conflict; unscheduled raceway 1/2 in minimum exposed and 1 in minimum embedded (¶1.01, ¶2.01, p.290) [Verified]. Raceway types (¶2.02, pp.290–291): galvanized rigid steel unless noted; liquid-tight flexible metal conduit to motors and vibrating equipment; UV-resistant Schedule 80 PVC above grade; Schedule 40 PVC underground with PVC-coated GRS sweeps and risers; PVC-coated rigid steel with 40 mil coating where called for [Verified]. Conduit schedule and tags (¶2.05–2.06, p.294): the drawing schedule governs sizing and routing, adjusted for equipment submittals at no added cost; crosslinked polyolefin tags, Impact Industries or equal (p.294) [Verified]. Handholes and tape (¶2.07–2.08, p.294): precast 3,000 psi reinforced concrete, galvanized checker-plate traffic covers for H-20 loading, solid slab bottoms with sumps and drains; detectable 2 in marking tape, red for electric lines (p.294) [Verified]. Conduit runs (¶3.01 A, p.294): no more than 270 degrees of bends between pull boxes and runs of 400 ft less 100 ft per 90 degrees of bend; no product submittal or test paragraph found in the section (pp.290–296) [Verified; submittal and test terms searched on every page].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 114), main spec pp.297–299; Wiki note 26 22 13 (Project_Wiki.md line 2081)
nodes.label: 26 22 13 · Dry Type Transformers
nodes.summary: Dry-type transformers 600 V and below for distribution, lighting and control; NRTL-listed; sizes and windings per the drawings; ANSI/IEEE C57.12.01 and UL 506; GE, Square D, Westinghouse or equal; equipment must fit the space shown (¶1.01–1.04, ¶2.01, p.297) [Verified]. Construction: 15 kVA and above with two 2.5% taps above and four below rated primary voltage; copper terminals in the bottom third; 15 kVA and smaller weatherproof non-ventilated and wall-mountable, larger indoor units drip-proof ventilated and 20 kVA and larger floor-mounted (¶2.05–2.08, p.298) [Verified]. Sound limits of 42 dB for 10–45 kVA and 45 dB for 50–150 kVA, and minimum efficiencies such as 98.0% for a 75 kVA three-phase unit (¶2.09–2.010, pp.298–299) [Verified]. Installation on rubber-in-shear or external vibration isolators with flexible conduit connections; each transformer is a grounded-neutral separately derived system bonded to the building ground grid; engraved phenolic nameplates (¶3.01–3.03, p.299) [Verified]. Submittals: catalog data per 26 05 00 (¶1.05, p.297); no test paragraph (the only "test" term is the NRTL listing) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 115), main spec pp.300–304; Wiki note 26 24 16 (Project_Wiki.md line 2091)
nodes.label: 26 24 16 · Panelboards
nodes.summary: Lighting and power distribution panelboards by Square D, Cutler Hammer or equal; submittals are catalog data per 26 05 00 (¶1.01–1.02, ¶2.01, p.300) [Verified]. Interiors: main ratings up to 600 A (main breaker) or 800 A (main lug), one fully rated plated-copper bus per phase, bolt-on breakers, suitable for service equipment where applied; thermal-magnetic trip-free main breakers (¶2.02 A–B, pp.300–301) [Verified]. Minimum interrupting ratings 10,000 AIC at 240 V and 208Y/120V and 25,000 AIC at 480 V and 480Y/277V; spaces fully bussed; surge arresters with indicators on all panels; schedules on the drawings (¶2.02 G–I, p.303) [Verified]. Execution: top of cabinet at 6 ft-6 in unless noted; typed circuit index; field quality control with inspection, phase load balancing within 20% and torque checks (¶3.01–3.03, pp.303–304) [Verified]. The E6.2 schedules show an SPD only at MDP (via E6.1); the spec adds surge arresters on LP1 and LP2 — drawings and specifications are complementary per 26 05 00 ¶1.011 B (pp.303, 274; plans_10 pp.2–3) [Inferred].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 116), main spec pp.305–311; Wiki note 26 24 19 (Project_Wiki.md line 2101)
nodes.label: 26 24 19 · Motor Control Centers
nodes.summary: Free-standing factory-assembled 600 V MCC furnished by the contractor with all related equipment; MCC sizes on the drawings are based on Allen-Bradley and "Motor control centers and VFDs shall be Allen-Bradley, no exceptions"; the contractor verifies fit before ordering (¶1.01–1.02, ¶1.05, ¶2.01, pp.305–306) [Verified]. Submittals beyond 26 05 00: wiring diagrams for every unit, component data sheets with part numbers, scaled arrangement drawings, wire marker text, bill of materials, 11x17 maximum shop drawings (¶1.04, pp.305–306) [Verified]. Construction includes NEMA 1 gasketed enclosures (NEMA 12 in damp or dusty areas), draw-out plug-in starter and feeder units, at least 5 spare terminals per unit, tin-plated copper bus with 600 A minimum horizontal rating, and a power monitor (¶2.02, pp.307–310) [Verified; pages scanned by key terms]. Execution: MCC completed and wired in the contractor shop and tested there with the control system, including every I/O point, control device and motor controller at rated voltage (¶3.01 B, ¶3.02, p.311) [Verified]. Consistent with E9.1 (Allen-Bradley Centerline 2100 IntelliCENTER); Add. 4 Clarification 4 sets the MCC at eight sections, 160 in (pp.306, 311; plans_12 p.3; Add. 4 p.1) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 117), main spec pp.312–313; Wiki note 26 27 26 (Project_Wiki.md line 2111)
nodes.label: 26 27 26 · Wiring Devices
nodes.summary: Receptacles, switches and other wiring devices: UL, NEMA WD-1, grounding type; 20 A duplex NEMA 5-20R (Hubbell 5362 or equal) indoors; GFCI (Hubbell GF-5362 or equal) where NEC 210.8 or local code requires (¶1.01–1.02, p.312) [Verified]. Outdoor, process and corrosive areas use corrosion-resistant duplex 20 A devices; 20 A switches with weatherproof neoprene plates in copper-free aluminum or PVC boxes; engraved phenolic plates naming panel and circuit (¶1.02 B–D, pp.312–313) [Verified]. Boxes independently supported and devices tested for correct connections (¶2.01, p.313) [Verified]. No submittal paragraph found in the section (term search on both pages) (pp.312–313) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 118), main spec pp.314–315; Wiki note 26 28 16 (Project_Wiki.md line 2121)
nodes.label: 26 28 16 · Disconnects and Switches
nodes.summary: Fused and unfused disconnects required by code for equipment under this and other divisions; NEC, OSHA and NRTL listing (¶1.01–1.02, p.314) [Verified]. Heavy-duty, horsepower-rated, quick-make quick-break switches opening all ungrounded conductors; NEMA-rated enclosures per the 26 05 00 area rules; fusible units with Class R clips only where the equipment manufacturer requires; Cutler Hammer, Square D, Westinghouse or equal (¶2.01–2.02, p.314) [Verified]. Mounting on corrosion-resistant Unistrut stands or walls with 1 in spacers off concrete or block, arranged by driven equipment, handle center at 4 ft 6 in (¶3.01, pp.314–315) [Verified]. Submittals: catalog data per 26 05 00 ¶1.012 (¶1.03, p.314); no test paragraph (the only "test" term is the NRTL listing) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 119), main spec pp.316–320; Wiki note 26 29 23 (Project_Wiki.md line 2131)
nodes.label: 26 29 23 · Variable Frequency Drives
nodes.summary: PWM VFDs for 480 V 3-phase, provided by the system integrator as a complete system integral to the MCC or other control panels; 1-year parts-and-labor guarantee from acceptance (¶1.01, ¶1.02 C, p.316) [Verified]. Submittals beyond 26 05 00: outline dimensions and elevations, wiring diagrams with all interface points and terminals, component and option data, and the operations and programming manual (¶1.02 A–B, p.316) [Verified]. Basic drive: pulse width modulated with a dual full-wave diode bridge converter (¶2.03, p.317) [Verified; section pp.317–318 scanned by key terms]. Quality assurance and start-up: each VFD functionally tested under motor load with simulated overload and 100% parameter verification; certified factory start-up for every drive with a start-up form, one week notice to the Engineer, and testing on both utility and standby power where a generator serves the load (¶3.02–3.03, p.319) [Verified]. Consistent with E9.2 (PowerFlex 753) and 26 24 19 ¶2.01 (Allen-Bradley VFDs, no exceptions); Add. 4 p.2 moves the sludge and 2W pump VFDs into the MCC, as the E sheets already show (pp.316, 306; plans_12 p.4; Add. 4 p.2) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 120), main spec pp.321–337; Wiki note 26 32 13 (Project_Wiki.md line 2141)
nodes.label: 26 32 13 · Diesel Emergency Engine Generators
nodes.summary: Basis of design Cummins C125D6D; pre-approved Cummins, Kohler, Caterpillar and Generac, equals if performance is shown; single-source package; 2-year warranty from Substantial Completion (¶2.01, p.325; warranty paragraph pp.324–325) [Verified]. Performance: NFPA 37, 70, 99 and NFPA 110 Level 2 EPSS; UL 2200; EPA Tier 3; noise within state and local limits at adjacent property lines (¶2.02, p.325) [Verified]. Sub-base double-wall listed steel tank with fuel for 35 hours at 100% rated power, sound-attenuated lockable aluminum housing (¶2.05 B, p.329; ¶2.08, p.332) — matching E10.3 (plans_12 p.8) [Verified]. Submittals: action, informational, closeout and maintenance-material submittals including fuel consumption at 0.8 pf and plans and elevations (¶1.04–1.08, pp.322–324) [Verified; pages scanned by key terms]. Field quality control and on-site acceptance: resistive load bank at full load with temporary connections, run at least 2 hours per NFPA 110; full fuel tank at final commissioning; at least 4 hours of training for up to 5 people (¶3.06–3.07, p.336; ¶3.09, p.337) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 121), main spec pp.338–348; Wiki note 26 36 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2151)
nodes.label: 26 36 00 · Automatic Transfer Switches
nodes.status: Main spec pp.338–348 · Header reads 26 30 00 — see conflict log
nodes.summary: Basis of design Cummins OTECSE with NEMA 12 enclosure and PowerCommand 40-01 controller; other makes acceptable only if approved at least two weeks before bid with a line-by-line compliance statement (¶2.01, p.339) [Verified]. Switches designated 3-pole get a neutral bus rated 100% of the switch rating; enclosures third-party certified to NEMA ICS 6 (¶2.02, p.341) [Verified]. Controller functions include a programmed transition of 0–60 s (default 3 s), test and exercise modes, and two normally open auxiliary contacts per position rated 10 A at 240 VAC; service entrance transfer switch requirements follow in ¶2.04 (pp.342–344) [Verified; pages scanned by key terms]. Submittals: action, informational and closeout (¶1.03–1.05, p.338); testing: factory dielectric test per NEMA ICS 1 and field tests and inspections by the manufacturer representative with reports (¶2.05, ¶3.03–3.04, pp.345–347) [Verified]. Consistent with E6.1 (400 A service entrance ATS, 4-wire 3-pole, NEMA 12, delayed open transition) and Add. 4 Clarification 5 (permanent ATS, temporary generator connects to it) (plans_10 p.2; Add. 4 p.1) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 122), main spec pp.349–351; Wiki note 26 51 19 (Project_Wiki.md line 2161)
nodes.label: 26 51 19 · LED Lighting
nodes.summary: LED lighting complete and operational per the plans and UL-listed; catalog numbers show design intent, and the written fixture schedule governs over fixture illustrations (¶1.01–1.03, p.349) [Verified]. Submittals: original product sheets, independent photometric reports where the schedule requires them, fixture types and project name marked, prepared by the local manufacturer representative, plus WSEC lighting control devices (¶1.06, p.350) [Verified]. Warranty: 5 years on LED products including parts and labor (¶1.08, p.350) [Verified]. Lighting controls (switches, contactors, occupancy sensors) where shown, compliant with the current Washington State Energy Code, tested and demonstrated as applicable (¶2.02, ¶3.01 I, p.351) [Verified]. Fixture mounting suited to the construction type and local seismic rules and coordinated with architectural ceiling plans (¶3.01 A–C, p.351) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 123), main spec pp.352–381; Wiki note 26 80 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2171)
nodes.label: 26 80 00 · Control System
nodes.status: Main spec pp.352–381 · Addendum 4: Add. 4 p.2, ¶2.04 D — Add. 4 governs · Header title differs — see conflict log
nodes.summary: Responsibilities: a system integrator (UL508A panel shop, AVEVA-registered, Allen-Bradley experience) designs, builds, programs and commissions the PLC panels and SCADA; equipment suppliers furnish packaged equipment for installation by the electrical contractor, program and commission it, give PLC tags and IP addresses to the Programmer, and supply UL or ETL labels per Washington L&I (¶1.04–1.05, pp.353–356) [Verified; pages read by key terms]. Major equipment (¶2.02, pp.357–358): MCC with VFDs; PLC panels — main PLC panel with operator interface, influent control panel, effluent flow meter panel, ventilation control panel; four floats each at the 2W and influent pump stations; level and pressure transducers; flow meters matching the E10.2 summary; DO meters; H2S and methane sensors; one heat/smoke detector in the Blower Building [Verified]. Instruments (¶2.04, pp.361–365): Orenco MF or Anchor Eco-Float floats; submersible level transducers; ASCO G2 pressure transducers; Promag L400 in ¶2.04 D, replaced by Promag W400 in Add. 4 p.2 (Add. 4 governs; the E sheets already show W400); Hach LDO probes with SC200 controllers; Sierra Monitor electrochemical H2S sensors; combustible gas detector; combination smoke/heat detector; door intrusion switch [Verified]. PLC and SCADA: Allen-Bradley CompactLogix, PanelView Plus 7 (2711P-T9W22D9P), DC UPS 1606-XLS240-UPS with a 26 Ah battery on every PLC panel, SCADA computer with a 750 VA UPS; after ¶2.05 the numbering restarts at ¶2.01 "SCADA Computer System and Equipment" (p.367) and ¶2.02 "Spare Parts" (p.370), so those are cited by page (pp.365–370) [Verified]. Execution: factory simulation witnessed by the Engineer and Owner before shipment, field acceptance test and operator training by the system integrator, then programming, start-up and commissioning; the description of operation sets sampler flow pace, the UV interface, generator and ATS status, and ventilation control, whose fan logic differs from E9.3 and E8.4 — see Issues (¶3.03–3.04, ¶3.08–3.09, pp.371–381) [Verified].

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 125), main spec pp.383–388; Wiki note 31 20 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2187)
nodes.label: 31 20 00 · Earthwork
nodes.status: Main spec pp.383–388 · Cites Sept 7, 2021 geotech report (p.383); Appendix C dates differ — Unresolved; flag: Merge exception report
nodes.summary: Covers excavation, hauling, disposal, backfill, compaction and final grading; cites the 'September 7, 2021' GeoEngineers report as Appendix C (¶1.01; main spec p.383 — Verified; date conflict already flagged, 02 Merge flag 2). Submittals: gradation and moisture-density curves for imported materials, separation geotextile data, and proposed compaction equipment; field density testing is by the Engineer's independent lab (one test per 100 LF of roadway, 1,000 SF of subgrade, 500 CY of structural backfill), with Contractor-paid retests (¶1.02–1.03; pp.383–384 — Verified). Crushed surfacing base course goes under all slabs and foundations: 12 in minimum for mat foundations and vaults, 18 in for shallow foundations, 24 in for pile structures (¶3.01 D; p.386 — Verified). Structural fill is placed in 10-in loose lifts and compacted to 95% MDD (ASTM D1557); unsuitable subgrade is over-excavated 18 in and replaced with CSBC on written authorization, with haul receipts to the Owner (¶3.03, ¶3.05–3.06; pp.387–388 — Verified). All fill materials are specified by WSDOT section (9-03.9(3), 9-03.10, 9-03.12, 9-03.14, 9-03.19 and others), and dewatering and boulder excavation are incidental (¶2.01, ¶1.04 B; pp.384–386 — Verified; material gradations Unresolved: external reference, not staged).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 126), main spec pp.389–392; Wiki note 31 23 19 (Project_Wiki.md line 2195)
nodes.label: 31 23 19 · Dewatering
nodes.summary: Covers dewatering of all excavations until backfill reaches finished grade (¶1.1; main spec p.389 — Verified). Submittal: a dewatering plan before construction, 'in accordance with Section 01 30 00', showing methods, equipment, well and sump details, stormwater diversions, discharge points and contingency plans for settlement; it is kept up to date like the TESC plan (¶1.2; p.389 — Verified; section number not in the manual, see Issues). Groundwater was monitored for ten months (Appendix B) and much higher levels are expected in winter; the section also cites the 'September 7, 2021' geotechnical report (¶1.3–1.4; p.390 — Verified; date already flagged, 02 Merge flag 2). The Contractor keeps backup pumps and a standby generator on site, dewaters at least 2 ft below any structure base, builds wells to WAC 173-160, and may not discharge to the sanitary sewer, outfall or WWTP (Part 2, ¶3.1–3.2; pp.390–391 — Verified). Testing: discharge is checked with a Rossum sand tester (10 ppm silica maximum) with 24-hour notice, and settlement reference points are observed near critical structures (¶3.2–3.3; pp.391–392 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 127), main spec pp.393–397; Wiki note 31 23 33 (Project_Wiki.md line 2203)
nodes.label: 31 23 33 · Trenching and Backfilling
nodes.status: Main spec pp.393–397 · Header wording — see conflict log
nodes.summary: Covers trench excavation, bedding, backfill and compaction for utilities, with the WSDOT/APWA Standard Specifications as the reference standard and 29 CFR 1926 for trench safety, which is solely the Contractor's responsibility (¶1.01, ¶1.03–1.04, ¶3.02; pp.393–396 — Verified; WSDOT/APWA Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Submittals: disposal sites, gradation tests and proctors for imported material, geotextile cut sheets, and a traffic control plan per WSDOT 1-10 (¶1.05 C, ¶1.06; p.394 — Verified). Trench backfill is bank-run gravel (WSDOT 9-03.19) and bedding is pipe-zone gravel (9-03.12(3)), with no native backfill or bedding; bedding is compacted to 90% MDD in 6-in lifts, backfill to 95% under paving or within 5 ft of roadway and 90% in landscaped areas (¶2.01–2.02, ¶3.03–3.04; pp.394–396 — Verified; conflicts with C7.4, see Issues). APWA color-coded 2-in detectable warning tape is required over every new utility (red electric, blue water, green sewer, orange telephone/CATV, light blue air) and replaced where existing utilities are crossed (¶2.03; pp.394–395 — Verified). Open trench is limited to 200 ft ahead of pipe laying and trenches are closed or plated daily; owner notice is needed for traffic or parking disruptions (48 hours for shutdowns) (¶1.05 B, D, ¶3.02 F; pp.393–396 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 128), main spec pp.398–400; Wiki note 31 32 11 (Project_Wiki.md line 2211)
nodes.label: 31 32 11 · Soil Surface Erosion Control
nodes.summary: Covers temporary erosion and sediment control under an Ecology Construction Stormwater General Permit (NPDES) whose SWPPP sets the requirements; the permit transfers to the Contractor at contract execution and the Contractor pays the yearly fees (¶1.01 A; main spec p.398 — Verified). Submittals: geotextile for silt fence, compost for compost berm, inlet protection products, barrier fence, track clean plates and any other erosion control product; the installer must be a specialist (¶1.04–1.05; p.398 — Verified). Products: silt fence to WSDOT 9-33 Table 6, straw mulch 9-14.4(1), compost 9-14.4(8), orange barrier fence 9-14.5(8), inlet protection per plans, specs and San Juan County catch basin insert requirements, and Track Clean construction entrance plates or equal per BMP C105 (¶2.01; p.399 — Verified; WSDOT materials Unresolved: external reference, not staged). All BMPs go in before land disturbance, stockpiles are covered with secured plastic, and areas stripped with no work for 14 days are stabilized immediately (¶3.01–3.02; pp.399–400 — Verified). The Contractor and Owner inspect BMPs periodically, the Contractor corrects impairments immediately and sweeps streets if soil migrates (¶3.03; p.400 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 129), main spec pp.401–403; Wiki note 31 40 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2219)
nodes.label: 31 40 00 · Temporary Shoring Bracing
nodes.summary: Covers temporary shoring and bracing for excavations, trench excavation safety systems under RCW 49.17 and WAC 296-155-655, and their maintenance (¶1.01–1.02; main spec p.401 — Verified). Where a trench box is not used or is inadequate, trench depth exceeds 4 ft and back-sloping is not used, the Contractor provides shoring designed, stamped and signed by a Washington PE; embedded elements must be drilled, not driven (¶1.03 B, ¶2.01; pp.401–402 — Verified). Submittals: shoring layout and design drawings, calculations and backup data, plus a settlement monitoring and contingency plan for excavations deeper than 10 ft (¶1.04; p.401 — Verified). The Contractor sets temporary benchmarks on adjacent structures, resurveys them weekly during excavation and stops work to implement the contingency plan if settlement is detected (¶1.05 A, ¶3.03; pp.402–403 — Verified). Shoring comes out in stages, damage from installation or removal is repaired by the Contractor, and the Owner takes no responsibility for trench safety (¶3.04–3.05; p.403 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 130), main spec pp.404–407; Wiki note 32 12 16 (Project_Wiki.md line 2227)
nodes.label: 32 12 16 · Hot Mix Asphalt Paving
nodes.summary: Covers HMA paving, restoration of all asphalt disturbed by construction, and temporary cold-mix (MC-2) patches, under the 2022 WSDOT/APWA Standard Specifications (¶1.01, ¶2.02; main spec pp.404–405 — Verified; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). HMA is Class 1/2-in PG 58H-22 per WSDOT 5-04.2 at 91% minimum density, commercial classification, with the mix design submitted on WSDOT form 350-042 and verified by WSDOT; lab certificates (sieve analysis, mix design) are due at least 5 days before placement (¶1.02, ¶2.01; p.404 — Verified). Asphalt is placed in 2-in lifts, matching existing thickness or the plan repair section, whichever is thicker; no material transfer devices; joints sealed with hot-poured sealant (¶3.02, ¶3.04; p.405 — Verified). The Contractor performs QC testing (asphalt content, gradation, voids, fracture, equivalence, in-place density) 'with Section 01400', which is not in the manual (¶3.05; p.405 — Verified; see Issues). Sawcuts are continuous, full-depth and pre-approved by the Owner in the field, trench patches extend 1 ft beyond the trench, and castings and monuments are referenced before removal and adjusted to grade (¶3.06–3.09; pp.405–407 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 131), main spec pp.408–412; Wiki note 32 32 23 (Project_Wiki.md line 2235)
nodes.label: 32 32 23 · Gravity Block Retaining Wall
nodes.summary: The Contractor designs, furnishes and builds the gravity block retaining wall; construction drawings and design calculations must be stamped by a Washington PE, with a manufacturer's certification before work starts (¶1.01, ¶1.04; main spec pp.408–409 — Verified). Units are Keystone Compaq II or approved equal to ASTM C1372: gray straight split face, running bond, 3,000 psi minimum, 8% maximum absorption, 8 x 18 x 12-in minimum, with two fiberglass pins per unit (¶2.02–2.03; pp.410–411 — Verified). The leveling pad (6 in minimum) and unit fill are crushed surfacing top course per WSDOT 9-03.9(3), and the pad is compacted to 95% standard or 92% modified Proctor (¶2.04–2.05, ¶3.02; p.411 — Verified; material Unresolved: external reference, not staged). The Owner's or Contractor's QA/QC representative inspects the excavation and tests foundation soils before the leveling pad; units are stacked no more than two courses ahead of fill, a footing drain and wall backfill are placed, and caps are glued (¶3.01, ¶3.03–3.04; pp.411–412 — Verified). As-built tolerances: ±1.5 in per 10 ft vertical and horizontal, batter within 2°, corners ±1 ft, gaps 1/2 in maximum (¶3.05; p.412 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 132), main spec pp.413–419; Wiki note 33 05 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2243)
nodes.label: 33 05 00 · Common Works Results for Utilities
nodes.summary: Supplements the drawings and WSDOT Standard Specifications for furnishing and installing all utility pipe and fittings, including trenching, over-excavation, bedding, backfill and trench dewatering; pipe must be new and sized as inside diameter unless it is a nominal-size product (¶1.01, ¶1.03; main spec p.413 — Verified; WSDOT Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Submittals: field-fabrication data, material certifications, and verification of every existing pipe to be connected (exposed and checked for size, material, elevation, location and service) (¶1.04; p.414 — Verified). Bolts and nuts are Type 316 stainless, thrust-block and tie concrete is 3,000 psi, and thrust restraint is not shown on the drawings and is incidental (¶2.01, ¶2.05, ¶3.018–3.020; pp.414–417 — Verified). Work near existing electrical and water services needs 3 business days' coordination with OPALCO, the Eastsound Water Users Association, the District and the Engineer (¶3.03; p.415 — Verified). Buried valves on ductile iron or nonmetallic lines get bituminous-coated nuts and bolts and an 8-mil polyethylene wrap; the section cites 'Section 01 30 00', which is not in the manual (¶3.025 B, ¶1.06 A.1; pp.414, 419 — Verified; see Issues).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 133), main spec pp.420–429; Wiki note 33 30 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2251)
nodes.label: 33 30 00 · Piping Systems
nodes.summary: General requirements for all piping systems shown on the plans, with trenching per 31 23 33 and submittals 'per Section 01 30 00' (not in the manual): field-fabrication data, shop laying drawings, pipe support drawings, material certifications and field welding procedures (¶1.01–1.02; main spec pp.420–421 — Verified; see Issues). Penetrations: poured-in-place DI wall pipe in slabs and walls, Link-Seal with 316 SS hardware (GPK sand collars for PVC) in new basins, core drilling in existing walls (grout at 6 in and under, Link-Seal at 8 in and over), and Link-Seal or Kor-N-Seal boots at precast manholes and vaults (¶2.01 C; pp.421–422 — Verified). All new piping gets #12 AWG steel-core tracer wire (Copperhead 1230-HS or equal) tied at 10-ft intervals, color-coded green for sewer, purple for non-potable and blue for potable, with Copperhead LD14/CD14/HS14 boxes whose locations are submitted before construction (¶3.03; pp.426–427 — Verified; conflicts with C7.1 and C7.4, see Issues). Testing is witnessed with 48-hour notice: force mains at 1.5 times operating pressure or 150 psi for 15 minutes (mixed liquor and West Plant Drain Pump Station force mains 150 psi, 2W and 3W piping 200 psi), HDPE per ASTM F2164, and valves with their pipelines (¶3.04.1–6, 8, 10; pp.427–429 — Verified). Gravity storm and sewer tests and water-line pressure tests and disinfection defer to WSDOT 4-04.3(1), 7-17.3(2) and 7-09.3(23), with DOH-lab chlorine (50 mg/L initial, 25 mg/L at 24 hours) and bacteriological reports (¶3.04.7, 9; p.428 — Verified; WSDOT test methods Unresolved: external reference, not staged).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 134), main spec pp.430–435; Wiki note 33 31 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2259)
nodes.label: 33 31 00 · Wastewater Piping
nodes.summary: Material requirements for wastewater lines, with installation and testing per 33 30 00 (¶1.01, ¶3.02; main spec pp.430, 435 — Verified). Footing drains are 4-in perforated corrugated polyethylene per WSDOT 9-05.2(7); gravity sewer and drains are PVC ASTM D3034 SDR 35 or DI per WSDOT 9-05.13 (Class 50/51, cement-lined, poly-wrapped), with Sch. 40 PVC drain pipe at 4 in and under 'or as noted on the plans' (¶2.01 A, C; p.430 — Verified; WSDOT materials Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Pressure sewer is DI, PVC C900/C905 DR 18 or HDPE; buried 2W/3W water is PE4710 IPS HDPE DR11; buried WAS discharge piping is DI; buried aeration piping 4 in and larger is poly-wrapped DI, with stainless steel below 4 in (¶2.01 B, D, E, F; pp.430–431 — Verified; conflicts with C1.3, see Issues). Each 1-in yard hydrant gets two 3/4-in x 50-ft fire hoses and each 2-in yard hydrant two 1.5-in x 50-ft hoses; exposed DI is epoxy-coated per 'Section 09900' and above-grade wastewater pipe is insulated (Trymer 2000 XP) with aluminum jacketing (¶2.01 J–M, V; pp.432–434 — Verified). Water and sewer lines near each other follow Ecology's Criteria for Sewage Works Design C1-9, and floor drain piping points to 'Plumbing Spec 22 10 00', which is not in the manual (¶3.01 F, ¶2.01 C.3; pp.430, 435 — Verified; see Issues).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 135), main spec pp.436–443; Wiki note 33 32 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2267)
nodes.label: 33 32 00 · Water Distribution Piping
nodes.summary: Covers HDPE, PVC and DI water main and appurtenances, chlorination, pressure testing and start-up, and as-built records per 01 70 00 (¶1.01 A; main spec p.436 — Verified). Submittals: field-fabrication data, material certifications, submittals for all pipe and appurtenances (fittings, valves, valve boxes, services), and a water main shut-down / temporary bypass plan with customer notices (one week for construction, 48 hours for shutdowns) (¶1.03; pp.436–437 — Verified). Buried potable pipe is AWWA C900 Class 235 DR 18 PVC or Class 50 cement-lined DI, both poly-encased fittings; potable service pipe is PE4710 HDPE (AWWA C901, ASTM F714) from continuous coil with fusion joints; cover is 3 ft minimum (¶2.02–2.03, ¶3.04 C; pp.438, 441 — Verified). Fire hydrants are Iowa or M.H. 929T with a 5-in Storz port, shutoff valve 5–20 ft away, crash posts where exposed, a 200 psi hydrostatic test and a flow test, and installation per 'ESWD Standard Detail W-1', which is not in the library (¶2.011; pp.439–440 — Verified). Testing and disinfection follow 33 30 00, and only Association staff may operate isolation valves on the existing system (¶3.05–3.06; p.443 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 136), main spec pp.444–446; Wiki note 33 33 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2275)
nodes.label: 33 33 00 · HDPE Piping
nodes.summary: Covers HDPE pipe installation; fusion operator qualifications go to the Engineer for approval before pipe is ordered (¶1.01–1.02; main spec p.444 — Verified). Operators must be manufacturer-trained with 5,000 LF of HDPE fusion experience, a comparable project in the last three years, and current 49 CFR 192.283/192.285/192.287 certifications for the machine used (¶1.03; p.444 — Verified). Pipe is PE4710 (ASTM D3350 cell class 445574C), DriscoPlex 4000/4100 IPS or equal, at the DR in 33 31 00 or on the plans, with color stripes: green sewage, light blue 2W, dark blue potable (¶2.01–2.02; pp.444–445 — Verified). Joints are butt-fused above ground to the manufacturer's procedure; all joints are visually inspected and data-logged (logs submitted), and 3 joints or 3%, whichever is greater, are destructively tested (¶3.03; p.446 — Verified). Pressure testing follows ASTM F2164 and Performance Pipe Technical Note 802 (¶3.04; p.446 — Verified).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 137), main spec pp.447–450; Wiki note 33 41 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2283)
nodes.label: 33 41 00 · Storm Utility Drainage Piping
nodes.status: Main spec pp.447–450 · Addendum 4: Add. 4 p.2, ¶2.02 — Add. 4 governs
nodes.summary: Covers new storm sewer pipe, catch basins, roof drains and retaining wall drainage; submittals are catch basins with frames, grates and lids, and storm and roof drain piping and accessories (¶1.01, ¶1.03; main spec p.447 — Verified). Storm pipe is double-wall corrugated polyethylene (ADS N12, Hancor HiQ or equal), ductile iron where cover is under 18 in, and CDF-encased where cover is under 1 ft; roof drains are PVC and wall footing drains are perforated corrugated PE with PVC tight lines (¶2.02 A, ¶3.02 D.7; pp.447–449 — Verified; WSDOT 9-05.20, 9-05.13, 9-05.1(5), 9-05.2(7) Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Type 1 and 1L catch basins, frames, covers and herringbone grates follow WSDOT 9-05.50(3), 9-05.15 and Standard Plans B-5.20-03, B-5.40-02, B-30.10-03, B-30.20-04 and B-30.50-03, installed per WSDOT 7-05.3 with frames on precast grade rings in a full mortar bed (¶2.02 C, ¶3.02 E; pp.448–449 — Verified; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Add. 4 adds ¶2.02 F: trench drains are Zurn Z886-HD or approved equal, HDPE channels with 0.75% built-in slope, 4-in inside width, 80-in minimum lengths with interlocking ends, black Dura-coated heavy-duty steel frames with embedment studs, and slotted ductile iron grates (5.375 in wide, about 18.5 sq in open area per LF) bolted after final inspection, Load Class C — Add. 4 governs (Add. 4 p.2 — Verified). Footing drain bedding, backfill and construction follow Sections 3.5 and 3.7 of the geotechnical report 'dated September 7, 2021', the Contractor provides construction layout staking, roof drains tight-line to catch basins with 12 in minimum cover, and removed storm sewer is fully removed or plugged (¶2.02 E, ¶3.02 B, F–H; pp.448–450 — Verified; date already flagged, 02 Merge flag 2; staking conflict, see Issues).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 138), main spec pp.451–452; Wiki note 40 05 71 (Project_Wiki.md line 2292)
nodes.label: 40 05 71 · Telescoping Valve
nodes.summary: One rising-stem 4" telescoping valve with at least 48" of travel on the aerated digester outlet, as indicated on the plans (¶1.01 A–B p.451). Construction: seamless stainless tube at least 1/8" thick on a stainless lifting bail; stainless companion flange with a neoprene slip-seal gasket at least 1/4" thick (ID 1/8" under the tube OD), 125# drilling to match the riser; handwheel lift at least 12" in diameter with UHMW thrust bearings, a self-locking 304 SS acme stem, a galvanized square-tube torque nut (or vee-keyed shaft) against rotation, and a clear butyrate stem cover with a position indicator in 1/4" increments; 316 SS pedestal on the concrete side wall with six 5/8"×5" stainless wedge anchors (¶2.01 pp.451–452). Basis of design is Waterman TS-2 or equal (¶2.02 p.452); submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data, fabrication and installation drawings, and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.451); installation follows the manufacturer's instructions and no testing is specified (¶3.01 p.452). The 48" travel matches the 21.3–25.3 T-valve operating range on C5.3 (Inferred check).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 139), main spec pp.453–461; Wiki note 41 12 13 (Project_Wiki.md line 2302)
nodes.label: 41 12 13 · Screw Conveyor System
nodes.summary: One complete screw conveyor system carries dewatered cake "from the rotary presses" to the final discharge point, with drives, motors, instrumentation, controls and supports, designed by the manufacturer to CEMA, AGMA, AWS D1.1 and AISC standards (¶1.1–1.2, ¶1.5 pp.453–455). The schedule (pp.460–461) lists two units: a "Receiving Conveyor" (horizontal, shaftless, 9" flight at 9" pitch, 6'-9" long, 304 SS U-trough 11 ga, two inlets from rotary press cake chutes, outlet to the inclined conveyor, Nord SK2282 SCP, 1 HP, 24 rpm) and an "Inclined Conveyor" (shafted, 9" flight at 5" pitch, 17'-4" long at 35°, 304 SS tubular O-trough 10 ga, outlet to bin, Nord SK2282 SCP, 5 HP, 53 rpm), both 0.5 wet ton/hr at 45% loading and 45 lb/ft³, with 3/8" UHMW liners and 2" drains. Troughs follow CEMA 300 in sections of 8 ft max, with UHMW wear liners in 4-ft pieces, a 2" stainless ball drain valve, anti-flotation devices every 16 ft on shaftless units and saddle supports at 16 ft max; drives are TEFC inverter-duty 1800 rpm motors on Nord shaft-mount reducers (AGMA Class 11, 1.4 service factor), with Siemens Sitrans WM100 zero-speed switches (120 VAC, NEMA 4X) wired to the PLC and interlocked with the MCC starter, and the conveyors run from the rotary press PLC and operator interface (¶1.8–1.13 pp.456–459). Submittals cite "Section 01340" and "Section 01 30 00" and repeat telescoping valve wording (¶1.3 A p.454; Issue 23), plus data sheets and component lists (¶1.3 B); each conveyor is shop assembled and run before shipment (¶3.02 A p.460).
