The two-conveyor, two-inlet arrangement does not match C6.1's single 28° conveyor from one press (Issue 22); Part 2 numbering runs 1.6–1.13 as printed.

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 140), main spec pp.462–471; Wiki note 43 11 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2312)
nodes.label: 43 11 00 · Blower Equipment
nodes.status: Main spec pp.462–471 · Pages numbered 431100-1 to -10, no total — see conflict log
nodes.summary: Four identical Kaeser Com-paK DB 166 C positive-displacement blower packages (20 HP, 460 V 3-phase, VFD variable speed) serve the Biological Treatment System from the Blower Building, and one Kaeser Com-paK BB 52 C (5 HP, VFD) serves the aerobic digester from the existing metal building just north of the proposed blower building, "just west of" and "adjacent to" Train #2; Kaeser, Aerzen or approved equal (¶1.01 A–B p.462; ¶2.01 A pp.462–463; ¶O p.469). Design points: 315 scfm at 8.9 psig differential per biological blower (325 icfm, 10.1 psig max, relief at 12.0 psig, 17.4 bhp, 3,999 rpm, 207°F discharge) and 120 scfm at 4.0 psig for the digester blower (124 icfm, 6.6 psig max, relief at 8.0 psig, 3.8 bhp), each in a 72 dB(A) sound enclosure (¶2.01 A; ¶P p.470). Packages are oil-free tri-lobe and belt-driven with automatic belt tensioning, integral inlet filter-silencer and discharge silencer, spring relief valve, flexible connector, pressure, temperature and filter differential gauges, TEFC IP-55 motors with PTC thermistors at 18–60 Hz, 100,000-hour L10 bearings and vibration to VDI 3836 (¶2.01 B–K pp.463–467). Each blower is slip tested and run 30 minutes at maximum speed and differential, each package runs 15 minutes before shipment with a conformance certificate, the blower warranty is 60 months from shipment (other components 1 year from substantial completion), and submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data, fabrication and installation drawings, and O&M information (¶2.01 L–N pp.467–468; ¶1.02 A p.462). Controls sit in a NEMA 12 cabinet with the VFDs in the MCC, and the contractor wires the over-temperature, over-pressure and motor temperature sensors to the PLC control panel and supplies tees, supports and fittings (¶2.01 Q, ¶3.01 A p.471).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 141), main spec pp.472–475; Wiki note 43 22 10 (Project_Wiki.md line 2322)
nodes.label: 43 22 10 · 2W Plant Water System Equipment
nodes.status: Main spec pp.472–475 · Addendum 4: Add. 4 p.2, ¶2.01 A — Add. 4 governs
nodes.summary: A complete 2W plant water system: two 2W pumps, pump station accessories, one fiberglass enclosure with a flow meter system, one fiberglass enclosure with an air gap system, two air diaphragm tanks, yard hydrants, wall-mount eye wash stations, and the piping and valving shown (¶1.01 A–B p.472). Base ¶2.01 A (p.472): two ITT Goulds 55GS50 4"-well submersible pumps with stainless components and Centripro M50434 5 HP 460 V 3-phase motors (or equal), 20–80 gpm, "Pumps are to include variable frequency drives (VFDs)", holding a constant user-set pressure (about 50–75 psi) and alternating after each on/off cycle; Add. 4 p.2 replaces the VFD sentence with VFDs in the Motor Control Center controlled by the PLC in the Main Control Panel — Add. 4 governs. Accessories are Orenco SBEX splice boxes, SBCS conduit seals, an MF2 float switch assembly with MFCOLLAR1 collars, HV discharge assemblies (2" with ball valve, check valve, flex hose and quick disconnect per pump), a PB30 pump basin and pressure relief valves each set at 110 psi (Clayton Mark or equal) (¶2.02 A p.473); the tanks are Amtrol Well-X-Trol WX-350D, 119 gal (26" × 62"), with relief valves at 100 psi on the tank tee and 120 psi on the pump discharge piping, a further 120 psi relief valve, a pressure transducer for pump on/off and a 0–150 psi gauge (¶2.03 A p.473; Issue 26). Exposed plant water pipe gets 1.25" closed-cell polyisocyanurate insulation (Trymer 2000 XP or equal) under a 26-gauge aluminum jacket, and exposed plant water piping, hydrants and pump discharge piping are labeled and painted per "Section 09 91 00" and Divisions 9 and 33, stainless pipe excepted (¶2.04–2.05 pp.473–474; Issue 27). Submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data, fabrication and installation drawings and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.472); one set of special tools is furnished (¶1.03 A); installation includes verifying pump rotation, and the suppliers train the Owner (¶3.01–3.02 p.475).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 142), main spec pp.476–480; Wiki note 45 05 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2332)
nodes.label: 45 05 00 · Valves
nodes.summary: Covers furnishing and installing the valves in the plant piping systems, complete with operators, with submittals per 01 33 00 and NSF 61 materials for potable water (¶1.01–2.01 p.476). Operators open counterclockwise; buried valves take AWWA C504 2" square nuts 18–24" below grade in two-piece cast-iron screw-type valve boxes (Mueller H-10364 or Clow F-2452 or equal) unless in a vault; gear operators keep handwheel pull at 40 lb or less, and butterfly operators show disc position (¶2.02–2.03 pp.476–477). Products: Kennedy resilient-seated NRS gate valves 2"–12" (AWWA C509/C515, C550 epoxy) and all-stainless NPT gate valves under 4" exposed; swing check valves with external lever, spring and limit switch (MH 259-02ALS, AWWA C508) and Tideflex TF-2M duckbill checks for vertical service; Pratt Ballcentric plug valves; Watts S-FBV-1 stainless ball valves under 4" for general exposed non-potable use and Asahi Type 21 CPVC true-union ball valves 2" and under for interior potable water; M&H Style 47 flap gates, demonstrated in dry and wet tests; butterfly valves — Asahi Type 57 PVC for interior PVC systems, Bray Series 31 lug or Dezurik for exposed ductile iron or stainless air piping, AWWA C504 Class 150B for buried water mains 10" and larger; A.R.I. D-025 combination air release valves; 2"-and-under globe valves (Issue 28); and Kennedy gate valves for buried plant water hydrant isolation (¶2.04–2.014 pp.477–479). Every shut-off or control valve gets a 1-1/2" stainless tag with its ID "as listed on the valve schedule", a submitted valve directory, and a label marker in a concrete pad per the plans and valve schedule (¶2.015–2.016 p.479); no valve schedule is in the P&M stack (cross-lane item). Installation sets stem orientation by pipe centerline height (4'-6") and requires watertight joints, and valves are tested with the adjacent pipeline, with a manufacturer affidavit on request (¶3.01–3.02 pp.479–480).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 143), main spec pp.481–485; Wiki note 46 33 33 (Project_Wiki.md line 2342)
nodes.label: 46 33 33 · Emulsion Polymer Make-up System
nodes.summary: One fully operational emulsion (liquid) polymer make-up system that activates and blends neat polymer (40–55% active) into a homogeneous 0.1–0.5% solution (¶1.01 A p.481). Components: a water pressure reducing valve set to 40 psi (supply 45–100 psi) with gauge; a proportional dilution-water valve (ball valve and positioner needing at least 90 psi air; flow "0.1 to 20 GPM (0.4 to 75 LPH)" as printed — Issue 29) regulated on the polymer-to-sludge ratio from the Rotary Press PLC, using the flow meter on the flocculator supplied with the press; a peristaltic metering pump (0.1–500 mL/min, up to 7 bar) with an inlet strainer; and a static mixer, on a 304 SS frame with HDPE water piping (Part 2 items 2.1–2.5 pp.481–482). Electrical: a 24 VDC, 4–20 mA proportional valve, a 120 VAC or 24 VDC pump with 4–20 mA control, and a NEMA 4X junction box with a 120 VAC/24 VDC supply, powered from a 120 VAC outlet or the Fournier control panel and run from the Rotary Press PLC and HMI in hand or auto (items 3.0–4.0 p.482). The materials list names Fournier Industries (frame, brackets), Watson-Marlow (dosing pump), Koflo (static mixer), Watts (regulator), Festo (proportional valve), Hoffman (10×10×8 junction box) and McMaster (valves, strainer, gauges, hose), with one metering pump head kit as the spare (items 6.0–7.0 pp.482–483); p.484 carries no text. Submittals cite "Section 01340" with telescoping-valve wording (¶1.02 A p.481; Issue 29), installation follows the manufacturer's instructions with no testing specified (¶3.01 p.485), and the liquid system conflicts with C6.1's "dry polymer mix unit" label (Issue 16).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 144), main spec pp.486–490; Wiki note 46 41 23 (Project_Wiki.md line 2352)
nodes.label: 46 41 23 · Submersible Mixers
nodes.summary: Furnish and install two mixer assemblies, two masts and two davit cranes, with one mixer in each anoxic zone of new Train #3 (¶1.01 A p.486). Mixers are at most 5 HP nameplate, 460 V 3-phase, with 316 Ti stainless propeller (EverClean blades), shaft, housing and frame, a duplex stainless casing cover, silicon carbide double mechanical seals in an oil chamber, a plug-and-receptacle power cable with resin-sealed entry, three PTC thermal switches and a moisture detector, bearings over 100,000 hours B10, maintenance intervals of at least 16,000 hours or 2 years, and 10 starts per hour (¶2.01 A–B, F pp.486–489). Each mixer rides a permanent 4"-square stainless guide mast with sockets at 10 ft max, a 14-position rotary top plate and an adjustable stop bracket (or a floor mounting pedestal), and two portable stainless lifting davits with manual brake winches mount on the top mast bracket, with removable handrail or chain sections so mixers need not be lifted over the handrail (¶2.01 C–E p.488); the mixer supplier furnishes motor-sensor monitoring relays that others install in the motor control panel (¶2.01 B.4 p.487). Controls follow 26 80 00 ¶3.09 B (¶2.02 p.489); submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data with wiring diagrams and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.486); the contractor gives a 1-year parts-and-labor extended warranty (¶1.03 A); three sets of wear parts are furnished (¶2.03); and testing covers factory checks (balance, leakage, electrical, insulation, no-load rotation), field testing after installation, 2 days of start-up and 1 day of training (¶2.04 p.489; ¶3.01 B–3.02 p.490). The same two mixers are also specified in 46 53 00, whose single-source and precedence clauses overlap this section (Issue 30).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 145), main spec pp.491–491; Wiki note 46 51 21 (Project_Wiki.md line 2362)
nodes.label: 46 51 21 · Coarse Bubble Diffusers
nodes.summary: Furnish and install coarse bubble diffusers as indicated on the plans; the only location listed is the aerobic digester (¶1.01 A–B p.491). Diffusers are 24" long, 316 SS, clog-free, open-bottom, with a rubber check valve in the air inlet against backflow of liquid or sludge, by Aquarius Technologies, SSI Aeration or approved equal, and removable from above the water line without entering the basin (¶2.01 A–B p.491). Submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data, fabrication and installation drawings coordinated with piping connections, and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.491); the contractor supplies tees, supports and fittings, installation follows the manufacturer's instructions, and no testing is specified (¶3.01 p.491). No quantity is given; G0.7 lists 6 diffusers at 20 cfm (Verified, plans_1 p.7).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 146), main spec pp.492–501; Wiki note 46 53 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2372)
nodes.label: 46 53 00 · Biological Treatment System
nodes.summary: Specifies Train 3 ("3rd Train") as a single bullseye multistage anoxic/aerobic activated sludge system, basis of design Smith & Loveless Model R Oxigest, with the in-basin aeration system, mixers, clarifier equipment, instrumentation and controls supplied and guaranteed by one manufacturer (¶1.01 A p.492; ¶1.03 A p.493); this section's valves, equipment, materials and controls supersede other specifications (¶1.03 F p.493), and alternate systems are bid as an Equipment Alternate with a submittal package (¶1.03 E, ¶1.04 p.493). Design influent is 63,333 gpd average to 178 gpm peak hour, with effluent BOD5 and TSS 30 mg/L and TIN 8 mg/L (¶1.02 p.492); the supplier gives a 2-year process performance guarantee with the equipment submittal and a 12-month mechanical guarantee from Substantial Completion (¶1.05 A, C p.494). The tank has a reinforced concrete outer wall and structural steel plate inner walls of at least 1/4" (¶2.01 B.1 p.494), 32 ft ID, 15.5 ft static depth and 16.9 ft overall wall height, 43,000 gal of annular aeration and 26,508 gal of anoxic volume in two compartments, each with a 5 HP 460 V submersible mixer, and 240 scfm through S&L medium bubble diffusers plus 75 scfm of airlift air, 315 scfm total (¶2.01 C.1 p.495; header and drop pipes ¶2.01 C.2 p.496). The 18 ft clarifier has 1.4 ft freeboard, a 1:12 concrete floor placed by the purchaser, an 800 ft-lb drive with a 1/2 HP 460 V motor, a scum airlift discharging to the aerobic digester and drive-failure alarm contacts; the system also includes a 3'-0" walkway, a 2'-0" service walkway, aluminum grating, handrail and ladder, a RAS airlift (51 gpm at 15 cfm, 3" riser), MLR airlifts (two at 101 gpm and 30 cfm, 6" risers) and carbon feed by two Stenner S3V02AA302N peristaltic pumps, 1 duty and 1 standby (¶2.01 B.2–B.3 p.495; ¶2.01 C.3–C.8 pp.496–498). Blowers are in 43 11 00 and air piping in 33 31 00 ¶2.01 D, the air header gets a 15 psi, 60-minute low-pressure air test (¶2.01 D–E p.498), and the manufacturer furnishes a NEMA 4X 316 SS control panel and spares and performs programming, start-up and a witnessed Functional Acceptance Test (¶2.01 F–G p.499; ¶3.03 pp.500–501).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 147), main spec pp.502–508; Wiki note 46 66 00 (Project_Wiki.md line 2382)
nodes.label: 46 66 00 · UV Equipment
nodes.summary: Two open-channel, gravity-flow, low-pressure high-intensity UV systems, each able to disinfect alone at max day 0.46 MGD, max month 0.22 MGD and minimum 0.03 MGD with TSS up to 30 mg/L, 33–85°F and UVT of at least 50% at 253.7 nm, to 200 FC/100 mL monthly and 400 FC/100 mL weekly geometric means, guaranteed regardless of influent count (¶1.01 A p.502; design criteria pp.502–503). Arrangement: 4 lamps per module, 6 modules per bank, 2 banks, 48 lamps (12 modules), in stainless channels furnished with the system, delivering at least 30,000 µWs/cm² (30 mJ/cm²) at 50% UVT after sleeve, fouling and aging reductions, proven by an independent bioassay to EPA/625/1-86/021, for outdoor installation without shelter (pp.503–504); basis is Trojan UV3000 PTP (base bid), with alternates bid as an Equipment Alternate and needing 500 North American installations, a bioassay and a 5-year guarantee (¶1.03 A p.502; Part 2 A p.504). Construction: 316 SS or quartz in contact with effluent; modules about 68"×20"×2.8", 38 lb, Type 6P, with electronic ballasts, 10-ft 120 V plug cords and LED lamp status; low-pressure slimline hot-cathode lamps warranted 12,000 hours non-prorated; Type 214 quartz sleeves; per-unit effluent channel with drain, module rack and downstream level control weir holding about 12" depth within 1.5" from zero to peak flow; two inlet and two outlet 304 SS transition boxes; a 304 SS maintenance rack; maximum draw 2,100 W at 120 V (pp.505–507). Monitoring: two submersible UV intensity sensors (one per bank, 10-year warranty), intensity and lamp-age displays and a low-UV dry contact in a fiberglass Type 4X wall panel less than 12 ft from the module LED end, plus GFCI duplex PDRs by the UV manufacturer, with the contractor supplying a 120 V circuit of about 19.2 A and a separate 120 V 5 A monitoring supply (pp.506–507). Submittals include shop drawings, electrical schematics, hydraulic calculations, bioassay and dose calculations and a lifetime performance guarantee (¶1.04 pp.503–504); equipment warranty is 12 months from substantial completion (¶1.05 p.504); spares are 4 lamps, 4 sleeves, 4 seals and an operator kit per bank (p.507); and the manufacturer provides 2 days of start-up and field testing and 1 day of training (¶3.02 p.508).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 148), main spec pp.509–509; Wiki note 46 66 10 (Project_Wiki.md line 2392)
nodes.label: 46 66 10 · UV Analytical Equipment
nodes.summary: Furnish and install one UV transmissivity analyzer, Hach Model DR 1900 (¶1.01 A p.509). ¶2.01 A, under the heading "UV ANALYZER", reads "The pumps shall be Hach Model DR1900" (Issue 34); standard replacement parts come with the unit (¶2.02). Submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data with wiring diagrams and O&M information (¶1.02 A); the contractor gives a 1-year parts-and-labor extended warranty (¶1.03 A); and the manufacturer provides installation certification, 1 day of start-up and field testing and 1 day of operator training (¶3.01). No location is given in the section or on the P&M sheets.

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 149), main spec pp.510–531; Wiki note 46 76 26 (Project_Wiki.md line 2402)
nodes.label: 46 76 26 · Rotary Fan Press System
nodes.summary: A single-source, shop-tested "plug and play" dewatering skid: one rotary fan press with one 36" dewatering channel, a flocculator, sludge manifold and piping, cake chute, an emulsified-polymer make-up system with dosing pump, an air compressor for pneumatic valving, screw conveyors (receiving and inclined "as needed" to reach the District's dumpster, as shown on drawings) and one control panel for the whole system, which also sets the digested sludge feed pump rate (¶1.0 A, C p.510; ¶1.7 p.514). Duty: at least 120 dry lb/hr from 0.5–2.5% solids at 5–25 gpm, producing 12–16% cake and up to 1,000 wet lb/hr, with design runtimes of 4.6–35.0 hours per week across current and 2040 cases (¶1.0 B, D, E pp.510–511); the press has a 1.5 HP 480 V TEFC drive, stainless hard-chrome filtration elements, six scrapers, a wash system limited to 750 gallons per 2.5 hours because "the 2W (air gap) water system has limited capacity", an LLDPE filtrate collector (7.5" outlet) to a 6" Sch 80 PVC manifold and LLDPE cake chutes (¶1.1–1.4 pp.512–514). The flocculator (model 05-300-900, 17 gal, 100 psi) has a 1 HP Nord SK0282 variable-speed agitator and a PVC air breather tied to "the potable water line", feeding the press through Sch 10 316 SS piping with Victaulic joints, 3" pneumatic feed and recirculation ball valves, lever channel isolating valves, 1" pneumatic wash valves and a 1" stainless polymer check valve, with the feed manifold shop tested at 100 psi (¶2.1–2.2 pp.515–518). Instruments and controls: E+H 10W 3" sludge and 10P 1" polymer electromagnetic flowmeters and a PMC71 0–30 psi pressure transmitter at the flocculator inlet, per-channel cake sensors and outlet air regulators, a wash-water pressure switch, and a NEMA 12, 480 V, CSA control cabinet with an Allen-Bradley CompactLogix 5370 PLC, PanelView Plus 7 HMI, PowerFlex 52X VFDs, an eWON Cosy 141 modem, a NEMA 4X press junction box and E-stop, programmed with the listed alarms, shutdowns and screens (¶4.1–4.4 pp.520–527). Submittals cover certified shop and erection drawings, electrical schematics and I/O diagrams, bills of material, spare parts lists and a detailed O&M manual (¶5.0–5.2 pp.527–530); the warranty is 1 year non-prorated from substantial completion (¶6.1 pp.530–531); there is no field start-up, field testing or training paragraph (Issue 37); and ¶1.1 cites "Section 22 13 16" for both the screw conveyor and the sludge pump (Issue 35).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 153), main spec pp.536–578; Wiki note Appendix C (Project_Wiki.md line 2419)
nodes.label: Appendix C · Geotechnical Report
nodes.status: Main spec pp.536–578 · GeoEngineers report dated Nov 8, 2022 (p.537) + report addendum dated Dec 16, 2022 (p.577); deferred (decision G): no text and no stored image, p.539, 576, 578
nodes.summary: GeoEngineers' revised report for 143 Cessna Road describes the site as fill (2–4.5 ft) over medium stiff to very stiff undifferentiated glacial drift (clay) to 19–24.5 ft, over glacial till, from borings B-1 to B-3 drilled Aug 10, 2020 (§§1.0, 2.3–2.4.1; main spec pp.542–543 — Verified). Groundwater in the B-3 monitoring well was 13.75 ft below grade (about El. 9.45 ft NAVD88) on Aug 24, 2020, with perched water likely in wet seasons; the report uses NAVD88 while the drawings use NGVD 1929 (§2.4.2; p.543 — Verified; see Issues). Design basis: Site Class D, not liquefiable, 2,500 psf allowable bearing on native drift or structural fill, settlement under 3/4 in, 6-in capillary break under slabs, and moisture-sensitive soils best worked in dry months (§3.0 summary; p.544 — Verified). Walls use 35 pcf active, 55 pcf at-rest and 300 pcf passive (drained), with an 18-in free-draining gravel zone and backfill compacted to 90–92%; structures get a perimeter drain of rigid perforated pipe (4 in minimum) in 6 in of 1-in washed gravel wrapped in non-woven geotextile (Mirafi 140N or similar), tight-lined to storm, and trench backfill compaction is 85% in landscaping, 90% below 2 ft and 95% in the top 2 ft under pavement (§§3.5, 3.6.2, 3.7; pp.548, 550 — Verified; conflicts, see Issues). The Dec 16, 2022 addendum suggests parking-area pavement of 2.5–3 in HMA over 3–4 in CSBC over 8–12 in gravel base, but its continuation page (p.578) and pages 539 and 576 have no text or image (p.577 — Verified; pages already deferred, 02 decision G).

nodes.citation: 02 Spec Index rev1 (line 156), main spec pp.611–620; Wiki note Appendix F (Project_Wiki.md line 2459)
nodes.label: Appendix F · Interim Plan of Operation
nodes.norm_label: appendix f · interim plan of operation
nodes.summary: Wilson Engineering's plan of interim operation lists the operational milestones from construction through start-up and states it is not part of the construction Contract Documents (§1.0–1.2; main spec p.614 — Verified). Scope summary: a third bullseye-style Bardenpho treatment train with new clarifier, an aerobic digester, UV disinfection, new dewatering equipment, a new influent flow splitter, new influent and 2W pump stations, a new blower building and stormwater improvements (§2.0; p.615 — Verified). Preliminary schedule: bid opening Feb 8, 2023, notice to proceed Mar 15, 2023, substantial completion July 2024 and final completion October 2024, with a CPM schedule due within 10 days of award and updated monthly per 01 31 00 (§3.0, Table 3-1; p.616 — Verified). Treatment stays continuous: the Contractor provides temporary piping from the existing chlorine disinfection chamber outlet to the 8-in effluent pipe just upstream of SSMH #1288, limits each disruption to 1 hour (influent pump station start-up with the flow splitter, the new 10-in effluent tie-in, the new transformer), lowers Train #2 with temporary pumps for the splitter tie-in, and submits a bypass plan; the detailed sequence is on C0.7 (§5.1–5.2; pp.618–619 — Verified). The Owner must have full use of the new generator before the old generator and switchgear are demolished, and at start-up new concrete basins get clean-water leakage tests and equipment gets operational tests per 01 45 00 and the equipment sections (§5.3.1, §6.0; p.619 — Verified).
